title: Baseline retest for cores/bench
Replace combinational 32-bit divider with a multi-cycle iterative divider
motivation:
The baseline Fmax is 5.4 MHz because the worst path (199.8 ns, 156 logic
cells) runs mem_wb.rd -> forward_unit -> EX forwarding mux -> alu -> BRAM
address, and that ALU path contains a fully combinational 32-bit
signed/unsigned `/` and `%` array divider. A radix-2 array divider is a
chain of 32 compare/subtract stages, which dominates every other path in
the design (the 32x32 multipliers map onto DSP blocks and are far
shallower). The timed circuit is therefore almost entirely limited by one
instruction class (DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU) that is essentially absent from the
timed CoreMark region (-O3 turns constant divides into multiplies;
list/matrix/state kernels use no variable divides). So the cycle-count
cost of making division slow is ~0, while the Fmax cost of making it
combinational is ~5x.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move division out of the combinational ALU into a small sequential
radix-2 restoring divider (new rtl/divider.sv, ~35 cycles per DIV*/REM*)
that stalls the pipeline at EX while it runs. CoreMark iterations/cycle
stays essentially unchanged (only a handful of divides execute, none in
the hot loops) while the critical path shrinks from the 32-stage divide
array to roughly the multiplier / forwarding-mux / ALU-add depth, which
should lift Fmax several-fold.

Design:
* divider.sv: inputs clock, reset, start-capture operands (a, b),
  is_signed, want_rem, `step_en` (= !dmem stall); outputs `done` and
  `result`. States IDLE -> PREP -> RUN(32) -> FIN -> DONE. Latch raw
  forwarded rs1/rs2 into the divider's own registers in the first EX
  cycle (needed because after >2 stall cycles the EX/MEM and MEM/WB
  forwarding sources are gone and ID/EX.rs?_val is stale). PREP takes
  |a|, |b| (negate if signed and MSB set) and records neg_q = sa^sb
  (when b != 0), neg_r = sa, dbz = (b == 0). RUN does 32 iterations of
  shifted = {rem, quo[31]}; if (shifted >= {1'b0,dvs}) rem = shifted -
  dvs, quo = {quo[30:0],1} else rem = shifted[31:0], quo = {quo[30:0],0}
  (33-bit compare so rem[31] is not lost). FIN picks quo or rem by
  want_rem and applies a single shared conditional negate into
  `result`; DBZ forces quotient = 0xFFFFFFFF and remainder = original
  dividend. INT_MIN / -1 falls out naturally (|INT_MIN| / 1 = 0x80000000,
  quotient sign positive -> 0x80000000, remainder 0), matching the RV32M
  spec exactly as the old alu.sv did.
* ex_stage.sv: compute is_div_op = in.valid && alu_op in {DIV,DIVU,REM,
  REMU}; ex_busy = is_div_op && !div_done. When ex_busy and no dmem
  stall, the EX/MEM register captures a bubble (reg_q <= '0) so nothing
  younger than the divide advances and the zeroed ctrl disables
  forwarding from the bubble. When the divider is DONE, the ALU result
  mux selects div_result (alu_result_final = is_div_op ? div_result :
  alu_result) and the instruction advances normally; the divider returns
  to IDLE on advance (!stall). For RVFI, rs1_val/rs2_val written into
  EX/MEM for a divide come from the divider's latched operands, not the
  live forwarding muxes (RVFI-only, pruned from the timed netlist).
  Under `ifdef RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS the divider is compiled out
  (ex_busy = 0, the existing XOR stand-ins in alu.sv are used), so the
  formal gate sees exactly the current combinational behaviour.
* hazard_unit.sv: new input ex_busy; stall_if |= ex_busy, stall_id |=
  ex_busy (ID/EX holds, same as the dmem-stall hold), flush_id gated by
  !ex_busy; EX/MEM holds only on dmem_stall as before. A divide in EX can
  never coincide with a redirect (it is not a branch/jump) so redirect
  priority in if_stage is unaffected.
* alu.sv: add `parameter bit HW_DIV = 1` guarding the `/` and `%` arms in
  the non-ALTOPS branch; ex_stage instantiates alu with HW_DIV = 0 so the
  combinational divider is not synthesized into the timed core, while the
  default (1) keeps test/test_alu.py's exact-bit divide vectors valid.
  Optionally collapse mul_ss / mul_uu / mul_su into one signed 33x33
  product (operands extended with a[31]&signed_a / b[31]&signed_b) to
  cut multiplier area and shared sign logic.
* core.sv: wire ex_busy from ex_stage to hazard_unit.
* test: add test/test_divider.py exercising the new module against the
  same RV32M divide/remainder vectors (div-by-zero, INT_MIN/-1, signed
  mixes, back-to-back, and a stall-in-the-middle case), and confirm
  cosim and riscv-formal still pass (ALTOPS path unchanged).

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-001-r1s0 (improvement, +735.15%): Fmax was set by a rarely-executed op (the combinational `/` `%` array divider in alu.sv, far deeper than any other path) while CoreMark's timed region has essentially no variable divides, so moving DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU into a multi-cycle divider that stalls EX (ex_busy -> hazard_unit, bubble into EX/MEM) cost ~0 CPI for a large Fmax gain — read the worst-path report for cold-instruction logic and make it multi-cycle before optimizing hot-path features.

title: Move M-extension out of the combinational ALU into a multi-cycle mul/div unit that stalls EX
motivation:
Fitness = iter/cycle x Fmax and the baseline runs at only 5.44 MHz: the worst
path is 199.8 ns / 156 cells through u_fwd > u_ex > u_alu. That path is the
single-cycle 32-bit `/` and `%` array dividers (plus three separate 32x32
multipliers, mul_ss / mul_uu / mul_su, all elaborated inside alu.sv and
hanging off the forwarding muxes). Every other path in this 5-stage pipeline
(fwd mux -> 32b add / barrel shift / compare -> redirect -> PC) is roughly
20-30 ns on GW2A. CoreMark at 2K executes only ~1.6k MULs and almost no
DIV/REM per ~449k-cycle iteration, so making M-ext ops cost 4-35 cycles
instead of 1 costs about 1-2% of iter/cycle, while removing the dividers from
the cycle-time path can multiply Fmax several times over. Cycle count is
essentially free to trade; Fmax is not.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a new module rtl/muldiv.sv and remove M-ext arithmetic from the EX-stage
combinational path. The pipeline topology is unchanged except that EX can now
hold for N cycles on an M-ext instruction, reusing the stall plumbing that
already exists for dmem_stall.

Design:
1. muldiv.sv (clocked, one instance in ex_stage). Inputs: the post-forward
   rs1/rs2, alu_op, `start` (= EX holds a valid M-ext op and the unit is
   idle, no dmem_stall), `advance` (= !stall_ex_mem, so the FSM freezes when
   dmem_stall freezes EX/MEM). Outputs: `busy`/`ex_wait` and `result`.
   Operands are LATCHED into a_q/b_q on the first EX cycle (the only cycle at
   which forward_unit's selects are valid for this instruction; later cycles
   see a bubble in EX/MEM and a moved-on MEM/WB), and the FSM then uses only
   its own registers.
2. Divider: radix-2 restoring (or non-restoring) iterative, 32 cycles, one
   33-bit subtract + mux per cycle (~4-5 ns). Signed ops take |a|,|b|, then
   fix up the sign of quotient/remainder. Preserve the exact RV32M corner
   cases already in alu.sv: x/0 = all-ones, x%0 = x, INT_MIN/-1 = INT_MIN,
   INT_MIN%-1 = 0.
3. Multiplier: ONE shared signed 33x33 multiply (operand sign-extension by
   op: MUL/MULHU unsigned, MULH signed x signed, MULHSU signed x unsigned)
   replaces the three 32x32 products. Pipeline it over about 3 cycles with
   registered stages (e.g. two registered 33x17 partial products -> registered
   sum -> select [31:0] or [63:32]) so no DSP chain + adder + fwd mux sits in
   one cycle. Alternatively a 4-bit/cycle shift-add multiplier (8 cycles) if
   DSP inference proves slow; either is acceptable (+1.5% to +3.5% cycles).
4. hazard_unit.sv: new input `ex_wait` (= M-ext op in EX && result not ready
   && !dmem_stall). It is a function of REGISTERS ONLY (id_ex ctrl + muldiv
   state), so it adds nothing to the redirect/imem_ready paths. stall_if and
   stall_id also assert on ex_wait (PC and ID/EX hold, as for dmem_stall);
   flush_id is unaffected (no redirect/load-use can coincide because the op
   in EX is not a branch/load). dmem_stall keeps priority over ex_wait.
5. ex_stage.sv: while ex_wait the EX/MEM register captures a bubble
   (valid=0, ctrl zeroed, so reg_write/mem ops are 0 and forwarding ignores
   it). On the cycle the muldiv result is ready, EX/MEM captures `result` as
   alu_result (mux added on the existing alu_result -> jump PC+4 mux, off the
   critical path since the result comes from a register). The ID/EX M-ext
   op is never squashed by anything older, so there is no kill case.
6. alu.sv: keep the M-ext cases for test_alu.py but gate them behind
   `parameter bit ENABLE_M = 1`; ex_stage instantiates `alu #(.ENABLE_M(0))`
   so synthesis drops the multipliers and dividers from the timed netlist.
   Under `ifdef RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS` the muldiv result must be the same
   (a+b)^K / (a-b)^K formulas as alu.sv, and the unit should use a short
   fixed latency (e.g. 2 cycles) so riscv-formal's ~20-step BMC depth still
   reaches M-ext retirements while exercising the stall/bubble plumbing.
   The real-arithmetic branch is covered by test_alu.py, cosim and
   make formal-deep; add a muldiv unit test (or extend test_alu.py with a
   wrapper) so the new FSM gets the same 30+ vectors/op.
RVFI is untouched: rs1/rs2_rdata come from the latched post-forward operands,
retirement order/valid are driven off MEM/WB.valid so bubbles do not retire,
rvfi_order stays +1 per retirement, and decoder/trap behavior is unchanged.

Expected result: the 200 ns divider path disappears; the critical path
becomes the normal fwd -> ALU/branch-compare -> PC path, projected at roughly
20-35 ns (30-50 MHz), i.e. several x the 5.44 MHz baseline, at a cost of ~2%
CoreMark iter/cycle. LUT4 count also drops substantially (divider and two
extra multipliers removed).

title: IF-stage predecode branch predictor: 2-bit bimodal BHT + JAL always-taken (zero-bubble taken branches)
motivation:
Today every taken branch and every JAL/JALR is only resolved in EX, and
the one wrong-path instruction fetched behind it is squashed, so each
taken control transfer costs a 1-cycle bubble. I replayed the CoreMark
(2K, -O3) retirement stream through the repo's Python ISS: 2.94M
instructions, 532k branches (296k taken = 55.6%), 49.6k JAL, 13.8k JALR.
Baseline penalty = 359k bubbles = 0.122 cycles/instr, i.e. ~8% of the
4.49M measured CoreMark cycles (CPI ~1.53). The Fmax-limiting path
(~200 ns, forward_unit -> ALU mul/div) is nowhere near the fetch path,
and in the timed netlist imem_data is just an LFSR register, so a
predecode -> 30-bit add -> PC-mux path in IF costs no Fmax. All of the
gain is IPC.

hypothesis.motivation:

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Predict control flow in IF, in the same cycle the instruction arrives
(imem_data is combinational from the PC register in this core and the
IF/ID bundle is not a flop). A correctly predicted taken branch/JAL
steers the PC for the very next fetch and loses ZERO cycles. A
misprediction is resolved in EX exactly as today (1-cycle penalty), so
the worst case equals the baseline taken-branch cost.

Measured predictor accuracy on the real CoreMark branch stream (offline
replay, per-branch outcomes at retirement):
  static BTFN                : 111.8k mispredicts (79% acc.)  -> loop exits hurt
  1-bit x64                  :  85.9k (83.9%)
  2-bit bimodal x16 / x32 / x64 : 71.0k / 56.0k / 52.2k (86.7% / 89.5% / 90.2%)
  2-bit bimodal x128         :  54.9k (aliasing noise, no better than x64)
  gshare x64, 4-bit history  :  65.0k (87.8%, worse than bimodal)
A return-address stack was evaluated and rejected: only 13.8k JALRs in
the whole run (0.3% of cycles) for ~120 FFs plus verification risk.
Residual penalty with x32 bimodal + JAL free + JALR unchanged is
(56.0k + 13.8k)/2.94M = 0.024 cycles/instr vs 0.122 baseline, i.e.
~0.098 cycles/instr (~289k of 4.49M cycles, -6.4% cycles, ~+6.9%
iter/cycle) at unchanged Fmax.

Design (if_stage.sv plus small EX/ID plumbing):
1. Predecode the MASKED IF instruction (the existing
   `(flush||redirect) ? NOP : imem_data` value) so wrong-path/stalled
   fetches predecode as NOP and never predict:
     is_jal = opcode 1101111, is_br = opcode 1100011.
2. Direction: JAL always taken. Branches use a direct-mapped bimodal
   BHT: 32 (or 64) x 2-bit saturating counters indexed by pc[6:2]
   (pc[7:2] for 64), reset to weakly-taken 2'b10; ~64-128 flops or
   LUT-RAM. Predict taken iff counter[1].
   Target = pc + (is_jal ? imm_J : imm_B): a dedicated IF-stage adder
   fed straight from instruction bits (no regfile, no forwarding).
   Do NOT predict taken if target[1] is set (misaligned target): leave
   pred_taken=0 so the existing misalign-trap path in EX is untouched.
3. next_pc = redirect ? redirect_target
           : (!stall && pred_taken) ? pred_target : pc+4.
   Keep redirect priority over stall exactly as now. When stall_if is
   asserted (load-use, imem or dmem stall) the PC holds and the fetched
   instruction is simply re-predicted next cycle; the BHT is read-only
   in IF, so no state is lost or double-updated.
4. Carry a 1-bit `pred_taken` (IF steered to pc+imm) through if_id_t ->
   id_ex_t (cleared on flush/reset like every other ID/EX field, held
   on stall). JALR is never predicted (pred_taken=0), stays as today.
5. EX: define `actual_taken = (branch_taken || (is_jump && !is_jalr)) &&
   !misalign_fault`.
     - Branch / JAL: `redirect = pred_taken ^ actual_taken`;
       redirect_target = actual_taken ? branch_target/jal target : pc+4.
       (JAL with an aligned target always has pred_taken=1, so never
       redirects; a mispredicted branch redirects to the correct side.)
     - JALR: unchanged (redirect unless misalign_fault, target =
       jump_target).
   reg_q.pc_next already carries the architecturally resolved next PC,
   so RVFI pc_rdata/pc_wdata continuity is unchanged. Redirect remains
   idempotent while a branch sits in ID/EX under a dmem stall (the
   condition depends only on ID/EX state), and a correct prediction
   issues no redirect at all.
   Why no wrong-path pollution: EX resolves the instruction immediately
   before the one IF presents, in the same cycle; any redirect that
   cycle masks the IF instruction to NOP and wins the PC mux. So IF
   only ever acts on instructions that are on the architecturally
   correct path.
6. BHT training: when a branch leaves EX (is_branch && in.valid &&
   !stall_ex_mem), write counter[pc[6:2]] toward branch_taken. Gating
   on !stall_ex_mem makes a branch held in ID/EX by a dmem stall train
   exactly once. The BHT is not architectural state; any initial
   contents are legal, so formal (liveness, pc_fwd, unique, ill) holds
   for symbolic BHT contents and the BHT may be left unreset if that
   infers LUT-RAM more cheaply.

Verification plan: cocotb/cosim diff against the Python ISS (retired
stream must be identical; only cycle count changes), `make formal`
(pc_fwd / liveness / unique are the checks that catch a
predict-vs-resolve bug), then `make timing`. Compare cosim cycles
against the 4,491,485-cycle baseline: expect ~4.20M.
Risk: the gain (~+6-7%) sits modestly above the 4.6% acceptance bar and
baseline Fmax seeds already spread 5.14-5.44 MHz, so placement noise can
eat part of it; keep the added logic minimal (no RAS, no gshare) to
avoid disturbing placement.

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-003-r1s2 (regression, +6.35%): The IF-stage predecode predictor (32x2-bit bimodal BHT, JAL always-taken, EX redirect = pred_taken ^ actual_taken) delivered its predicted ~6% as a pure IPC gain (fitness 12.89 vs 12.12) but was measured on the pre-divider ~5.4 MHz baseline, so it scored as a regression once the divider win moved the head to ~101 — the "costs no Fmax" argument only held while the 200 ns ALU divider path hid the new predecode -> 30-bit add -> PC-mux fetch path, so re-propose it rebased on the current head and check that path against the ~28 ns critical path before counting on Fmax-neutrality.

title: Take late EX redirect off the IF NOP-mask / load-use compare / ID-EX flush chain
motivation:
I ran `make timing TARGET=bench` on the current head and read the full Gowin
report (core_bench.tr). Path 1..25 are all the same structure, 28.396 ns
arrival, 21 logic levels, ending on RESET pins of the ID/EX data flops
(id_ex_w.rs1_val_*/rs2_val_*), setup relation 5 ns -> period 23.1 ns = 43.3 MHz.
Annotated path (times are arrival ns; launch is at 5.33):
  BSRAM DO (ID/EX rs?_val, c2q 2.26)                         7.6
  4 LUT levels: regfile bypass + EX forwarding mux           12.7
  32-bit compare carry chain (BLT/BGE/BEQ...)                15.1
  4 LUT levels in u_if/n69_*: branch_cond -> `redirect`      19.7  (fanout 101)
  u_if rs2_addr_w_2: the IF NOP-mask `(flush||redirect)?NOP:imem_data` 21.3
  u_hazard n12..n14: 5-bit load-use compare (carry cells)    23.2
  5 LUT levels u_id: flush_id/stall_id/reset combine         26.99 (fanout 33)
  route to RESET of ID/EX flops                              28.4
So 8.7 of the 14.4 ns after launch are spent AFTER `redirect` is known, and
almost all of it is redundant: (1) `redirect` is only used to force the fetched
instruction to a NOP before it reaches decoder / regfile address pins / load-use
compare, but a redirecting EX instruction (branch/jal/jalr) always has

       depend on `redirect`, deleting the 21.3 -> 23.2 -> 24.2 legs (~4-5 ns)
       and cutting the 101-fanout net on `redirect`.

       but never latched, because flush_id = redirect && !dmem_stall &&
       !ex_busy clears ID/EX, and when dmem_stall/ex_busy hold ID/EX the IF
       output is ignored exactly as before. load_use_hazard is provably 0 when
       redirect=1 (the redirecting instruction is a branch/jump, mem_read=0),
       so stall_if/stall_id/flush_id are unchanged. PC update keeps
       `redirect` priority over `stall`.
2. hazard_unit.sv: restructure so the late `redirect` enters the flush as a
   single AND-OR: `hold = dmem_stall || ex_busy` (early),
   `flush_id = (redirect && !hold) || (load_use_hazard && !hold)`,
   `stall_id = hold || load_use_hazard`. Same function, but the synthesizer
   sees redirect as the last input of a 1-2 level cone instead of 5 levels.

   ctrl fields); the wide data fields (pc, rs1_val, rs2_val, imm, rd,
   rs1_addr, rs2_addr, instr) load on !stall and are never cleared. A bubble

   ctrl), redirect (is_branch/is_jump=0) or trigger load-use (mem_read=0), and
   RVFI fields are only observed when valid=1. This cuts the late flush net

   path flops (and the BSRAM-absorbed rs?_val registers) free of reset logic.

   (stall ? pc : pc + 4)` so only one 2:1 mux level follows `redirect`.

title: Break the EX redirect -> IF/ID NOP-gate -> hazard compare -> ID/EX clear loop
motivation:
`make timing` on the current head (43.3 MHz at placement option 0) shows
the 28.4 ns worst path in full. It is NOT a plain regfile read. The cell
trace is: regfile BSRAM DO (ID/EX rs2_val) at 7.6 ns -> bypass LUT ->
EX forwarding mux (3 LUT levels, arrives 12.7 ns) -> 32-bit branch
comparator carry chain (15.1 ns) -> 4 LUT levels of `redirect` logic in
u_if (n69_*, arrives 19.7 ns, fanout 101) -> gated IF/ID instruction bits
(rs?_addr_w, 21.3 ns, fanout 12) -> hazard_unit load-use 5-bit compare
carry chain (23.2 ns) -> stall/flush LUTs in id_stage (26.4-27.0 ns,
fanout 33) -> synchronous RESET pins of the ~180 ID/EX flops (28.4 ns).
So roughly 8.7 ns of the path (19.7 -> 28.4) is spent AFTER `redirect` is
known, serialising redirect -> instruction NOP-gate -> load-use compare ->
flush_id -> ID/EX reset. That tail exists only because if_stage computes
`out.instr = (flush || redirect) ? NOP : imem_data` and the hazard unit's
load-use compare reads that gated instruction. The gate is functionally
redundant for redirects: flush_id already zeroes ID/EX on every redirect
(flush_id = (load_use|redirect) & !dmem_stall & !ex_busy and id_stage's
`if (reset || flush)` has priority over stall), and when dmem_stall holds
ID/EX the wrong-path instruction is simply not captured. Earlier
experiments (multi-cycle MUL, branch predictor) did not touch this loop,
which is why the head sat at ~45 MHz.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make the IF->ID bundle independent of `redirect`.
1. hazard_unit: flush_if = imem_stall only (drop `redirect ||`).
2. if_stage: out.instr = flush ? NOP : imem_data and out.valid = !flush;
   the `redirect` input is kept only for the PC mux / PC enable priority
   over stall (already `else if (redirect) pc <= redirect_target`).
After this the load-use compare, the regfile read address, decoder and
imm_gen all hang off `imem_data`/`imem_ready` (flop-driven), never off
`redirect`. `redirect` then only drives (a) the PC mux/enable and (b)
flush_id -> the ID/EX clear, i.e. about 2 LUT levels + the reset net after
the compare instead of ~8.7 ns of serial logic.
Why this is functionally safe (all verified by reading the RTL):
- Redirect cycle, no stall: ID/EX is cleared by flush_id, so the wrong-path
  instruction that is combinationally in ID is never captured; PC takes the
  target. A spurious load-use computed on the wrong-path instruction only
  asserts stall_if/stall_id; stall_if is overridden by redirect in the PC
  always_ff and stall_id loses to flush in id_stage.
- Redirect cycle with dmem_stall: stall_id holds ID/EX (flush_id is gated
  by !dmem_stall), exactly as today, and the held EX branch keeps
  redirecting until the stall releases, then flushes. The IF/ID bundle
  content is irrelevant while ID/EX holds.
- ex_busy (divide) never coincides with a redirect.
- imem_stall still turns the IF/ID bundle into NOP with valid = 0.
Retirement/RVFI order is unchanged because bubbles appear on exactly the
same cycles as before (CPI identical); only the timing of the combinational
path changes. The remaining worst path should be DO -> forward mux ->
comparator -> redirect -> (PC mux | ID/EX clear), about 17-18 ns of logic
(vs 23 ns now), i.e. ~55-58 MHz (+25-30% over 43-45 MHz).
Optional follow-ups for the implementer, only if the post-change
`make timing` still shows the redirect cone as the head:
(a) precompute the branch/JAL target-misalignment flag in ID (depends only
    on pc and imm, not on rs1) and register it in ID/EX so the 4-level
    `redirect` LUT cone (branch_cond mux, misalign_branch, misalign_jump)
    shrinks to ~2 levels; keep JALR's low-two-bit misalign check in EX.
(b) clear only valid + side-effecting ctrl bits (reg_write, mem_read,
    mem_write, is_branch, is_jump) on flush so the high-fanout RESET is
    not applied to the 32-bit data fields (pc, rs?_val, imm, instr).
Neither follow-up may weaken trap/misalign semantics (invariants 2, 10);
riscv-formal's pc_fwd/ill checks must still pass.

title: IF-stage bimodal+JAL predictor rebased on divider head, with redirect cone decoupled from fetch/hazard
motivation:
Every taken branch / JAL is resolved in EX and squashes the one wrong-path
instruction sitting in ID (the IF/ID bundle is combinational off the PC reg),
so each costs a 1-cycle bubble. Replaying CoreMark (2K, -O3) through the repo
ISS: 2.94M instrs, 532k branches (55.6% taken), 49.6k JAL, 13.8k JALR ->
~359k bubbles of ~4.49M cycles (~8%). The r1s2 attempt (32x2-bit bimodal BHT,
JAL always-taken, redirect = pred ^ actual) passed formal+cosim and cut
cycles 4,491,817 -> 4,203,461 (-6.4%, +6.9% iter/cycle) but was scored against
the old 5.4 MHz baseline, where the 200 ns divider path hid its Fmax cost, so
it showed up as a "regression" once the divider win moved the head to 101.22.
This is the rebase the lesson asked for: the IPC gain is real and has to be
delivered without lengthening the ~28 ns critical path.
The current worst path (28.4 ns, 21 levels, modules u_ex -> u_if -> u_hazard
-> u_id) is the REDIRECT cone: EX branch compare -> `redirect` -> if_stage
instr NOP-mask -> hazard_unit load-use comparators -> stall_id/flush_id ->
ID/EX enable/reset. That dependence is logically redundant (a masked NOP has
rs1=rs2=0, and flush_id already ORs in `redirect`), so it can be cut.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Part A (the predictor, same design as the measured r1s2 but built to be
timing-clean on the new head):
1. if_stage predecodes the RAW imem_data (not the redirect-masked value, so
   redirect is not on the predecode/adder cone): is_jal = opcode 1101111,
   is_br = opcode 1100011. Direction: JAL always taken; branches use a
   direct-mapped 32 x 2-bit bimodal BHT indexed by pc[6:2], reset to weakly
   taken (2'b10), predict taken iff counter[1]. Target = pc + (is_jal ?
   imm_J : imm_B), a dedicated IF adder fed straight from instruction bits.
   Never predict taken when target[1] is set (misaligned target) so the
   existing misalign-trap path in EX is untouched.
2. PC update priority is unchanged and redirect wins over everything:
   pc <= redirect ? redirect_target : !stall ? (pred_taken ? pred_target :
   pc+4) : pc. pred_taken is forwarded in a new 1-bit if_id_t / id_ex_t field
   qualified with !stall_if and the instruction's valid (zero for
   flush/redirect/imem-stall bubbles). Any real branch/JAL that is captured
   into ID/EX had stall_if=0 (stall_if implies stall_id), so its prediction
   really steered the PC.
3. ex_stage: actual_taken = is_jump | branch_taken; redirect =
   (actual_taken ^ pred_taken) && !misalign_fault; redirect_target =
   is_jump ? jump_target : branch_taken ? branch_target : pc+4. JALR still
   always redirects (pred is 0 for it). pc_next / rvfi pc_wdata semantics
   are unchanged (still the actual next PC).
4. BHT training is taken OFF the critical path: it is driven from the EX/MEM
   register (ex_mem_w.ctrl.is_branch && valid, ex_mem_w.pc[6:2],
   ex_mem_w.branch_taken), one cycle after resolve, as a read-modify-write
   saturating inc/dec on a second read port. A branch sitting in EX/MEM is
   never a dmem-stalled op, so it trains exactly once. Starting from flops,
   no late branch-compare signal reaches the BHT D inputs.
Part B (supporting change that keeps Part A Fmax-neutral and likely
Fmax-positive): break the redundant redirect -> NOP-mask -> hazard/regfile
address dependence. core.sv feeds hazard_unit.if_id_rs1/rs2 and id_stage's
regfile read addresses from the raw imem_data[19:15]/[24:20] instead of the
masked instr. Safe because: on redirect, flush_id is already 1 (unless
dmem_stall/ex_busy, in which case stall_id is already 1) and the PC takes
redirect_target regardless of stall_if, so a spurious load-use during a
redirect changes nothing; on imem_stall a spurious load-use only turns
"capture a valid=0 NOP bubble" into "capture a zero bubble", equivalent
because stall_if is already 1; for any valid instruction raw == masked, and
a bubble's rs?_val is never consumed (valid=0, rd=0, is_branch=0). ID/EX
rs1_addr/rs2_addr/instr/ctrl stay on the masked instruction.
Expected: cycles -6.4% (+6.9% iter/cycle) from Part A; the r1s2 netlist had
no Fmax penalty at 5 MHz and the new fetch path (lfsr/imem_data -> opcode
match + BHT bit -> 30-bit carry add -> 2:1 PC mux, ~8-10 levels) is well
below the 21-level 28 ns head; Part B removes ~4-6 levels (mask -> 5-bit
compares -> stall OR -> reg enable) from that head path, so Fmax should be
flat-to-up. Area: ~64 BHT FFs + ~50 LUT for the adder/predecode/train logic
(2458 -> ~2650 LUT4 of 10000).

title: Cut the EX late-arrival tail: DSP product enters a one-hot final mux, dedicated load/store address adder, data-field ID/EX flops free of flush
motivation:
I ran `make timing TARGET=bench` on the current head (place_option 0: 51.63 MHz,
worst path 24.663 ns, 15 cells) and read core_bench.tr. 24 of the 25 reported
paths are one path family, and path 3 ties it to 0.02 ns:
(A) 24.663 ns, endpoints dmem_*_dmem_*/ADB[*] (the dmem BSRAM address): regfile
    BSRAM DO 7.59 -> 2 bypass LUTs (9.3) -> 2 EX forward-mux LUTs (11.0) ->
    alu_a mux (12.5, fanout 24) -> mul_a_32 (33rd operand bit, 14.0) -> DSP
    multiplier mul_p (3.76 ns, out at 18.4) -> SEVEN chained LUTs

title: Dedicated load/store address adder in EX, decoupled from the ALU result mux and DSP multiplier
motivation:
After the divider and the IF-stage predictor merged, every recent run (r2s0,
r2s1, r2s2) lands on the same ~25 ns wall: regfile BSRAM (ID/EX rs?_val) ->
EX forwarding mux -> u_alu -> alu_result_final -> dmem BSRAM address pin,
14-15 logic cells in modules u_id/u_ex/u_alu. The dmem array in the timed
wrapper is a combinational-read RAM, so synthesis folds the EX/MEM
alu_result register into the BSRAM address register and the whole EX stage
(forward mux, alu operand mux, 32-bit adder, the ~19-way case(op) result mux
that also carries the shared 33x33 DSP product and shifter, plus the
JAL/divide alt_sel mux) becomes one path that ends on a BSRAM address pin
(which also has a bigger setup than a plain flop). For a load/store the
only thing that is needed on that pin is rs1 + imm; everything else in the
ALU result mux (SLT, shifts, MUL/MULH, LUI, JAL link, divider result) is
irrelevant to the address but still sits in front of it.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a dedicated address-generation adder in ex_stage: mem_addr = rs1_fwd +
in.imm (no auipc mux, no alu_src mux, no ALU op mux, no alt_sel mux). Carry
it in a new ex_mem_t field (mem_addr) and drive mem_stage's dmem_addr, the
byte-lane mask / misalign check / aligned RVFI address and the load-extract
shift from that field instead of alu_result. alu_result keeps its current
role for writeback/forwarding of non-memory instructions (a load's
alu_result slot is never consumed because mem_to_reg selects read_data, and
a store has no rd, so the redundant ALU copy of the address is simply not
used for forwarding). Because only the mem_addr register feeds the dmem
address pins, synthesis absorbs THAT register into the BSRAM address
register and the path to the BSRAM is just: BSRAM DO -> 3:1 forward mux ->
carry-chain adder -> BSRAM address, i.e. several LUT levels shorter, while
the remaining ALU paths now end at ordinary flops with smaller setup and no
BSRAM routing. To keep the ALU-to-flop paths from becoming the new wall,
also pre-decode alu_op in ID into a small one-hot result-class select
(arith/logic, shift, slt, mul, link/div) stored in ctrl so the EX result mux
is an AND-OR of already-registered selects instead of a 5-bit case decode.
No behavioural or CPI change: same cycle count, same RVFI values (mem_addr
for RVFI still equals the word-aligned effective address, and the
misaligned-access trap uses the same low address bits).

title: Flatten the EX operand-forward network: ID-stage one-hot forward selects (registered), regfile bypass folded in as a WB2 source, AND-OR mux
motivation:
I ran `make timing TARGET=bench` on the current head (option 0, 63.6 MHz,
period ~15.7 ns) and read core_bench.tr. The top paths are two families that
tie at ~21.0 ns arrival and share the same front end:
  (A) BSRAM DO (regfile = ID/EX rs?_val, launch 7.59) -> 4 serial LUTs
      (regfile write-first/x0 bypass LUT `id_ex_w.rs?_val_*_s15` 8.46, then
      three EX forward-mux LUTs `alu_b_2_s3/alu_b_2_s1/rs2_2_s8` or
      `rs1_25_s9/s8/s10`, ~4.5 ns total, 12.09) -> either the 32-bit branch
      compare carry chain -> `redirect` -> pc CE (pc_21, 21.02), or alu_a
      mux -> ALU -> EX/MEM.alu_result flop (21.01).
After the last merged wins nothing downstream of that front end is deeper
than it: the compare->redirect->pc leg is ~8.9 ns and the ALU->flop leg
~9 ns. The 4-LUT / 4.5 ns operand front end is paid on every EX path, and
its selects (fwd_rs1_sel/fwd_rs2_sel) are built in EX from 5-bit register
number compares and a priority chain, so they arrive about as late as the
BSRAM data and the mux is also forced into a cascade (data enters LUT 1,
LUT 2, LUT 3 in series) instead of one wide select.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Pay for operand selection once, in ID, off the critical path, and make the
EX operand mux a flat AND-OR of flop/BSRAM outputs with already-registered
one-hot selects (2 LUT levels instead of 4, ~-2 ns on both worst-path
families, i.e. ~13% period if the next paths sit near 19 ns).

1. In id_stage (cycle t, instruction I in IF/ID, raw rs1/rs2 fields a):
   compare a against the three producers visible at t and register, per
   operand, a one-hot select that is valid for I's first EX cycle (the
   pipeline advances exactly one slot when ID/EX captures, because ID/EX
   only loads when !stall_id, i.e. no dmem stall / load-use / ex_busy):
      sel_ex   : a == id_ex.rd  & reg_write(after misalign-jump trap)   -> EX/MEM.alu_result | mul_q at t+1
      sel_wbl  : a == ex_mem.rd & reg_write(after mem-misalign trap) & mem_to_reg  -> MEM/WB.read_data
      sel_wba  : a == ex_mem.rd & reg_write(after trap) & !mem_to_reg               -> MEM/WB.alu_result
      sel_wb2  : a == mem_wb.rd & w_en (producer being written this cycle; replaces the regfile write-first bypass) -> wb2_q (new 32-bit flop of wb_w_data, loaded every cycle that mem_wb is valid)
      sel_ram  : a != 0 and none of the above                            -> BSRAM/ID-EX rs?_val
   Priority is the existing one (youngest producer wins, x0 reads 0 because
   all selects are 0). Selects are enabled by the same !stall_id as the
   other ID/EX data flops (no flush needed: a bubble's operands are dead).
   Priority/trap gating are computed here from flops, so they only feed flop
   D inputs.
2. reg_file: drop the write-first bypass and the x0 mux from the read ports
   (plain registered-style read, x0 handled by sel_ram=0); this removes the
   bypass LUT that Gowin currently places after the BSRAM DO pins. Keep the
   reset-clear and w_addr != 0 write guard so the formal/cosim semantics and
   reg x0 == 0 invariant are unchanged. (Verify with `make timing` that the
   regfile still maps to BSRAM with the ID/EX rs?_val as its output register.)
3. ex_stage: replace the case(fwd_sel) muxes with
      rs1 = ({32{sel_ram}} & in.rs1_val) | ({32{sel_wb2}} & wb2_q)
          | ({32{sel_ex}} & reg_q.alu_result) | ({32{sel_ex}} & mul_q)
          | ({32{sel_wbl}} & mem_wb.read_data) | ({32{sel_wba}} & mem_wb.alu_result)
   (same for rs2). The AND-OR has 6 terms (3 LUT4 + 1 OR LUT = 2 levels) and
   the selects come straight from flops. forward_unit.sv becomes unused for
   the datapath (delete or keep only for RVFI).  ALU operand select, branch
   compare and jalr adder keep using rs1/rs2 unchanged, so ex_stage's late
   legs are untouched and the compare->redirect->pc leg and the
   ALU->alu_result leg both start ~2 ns earlier.
4. Stall consistency: ID/EX rs?_val, the select flops and wb2_q all hold on
   the same stall conditions the existing registers hold on; during a dmem
   stall MEM/WB data fields are retained (hold_wb keeps them), so
   sel_wbl/sel_wba stay valid for as long as the consumer is held in EX,
   exactly as the dynamic compare does today. Bubbles clear ctrl/valid so
   producers in EX/MEM are never forwarded from when invalid.
Risk: the select-decode logic is new; riscv-formal (pc_fwd, reg, liveness)
and cosim fully cover forwarding, including load-use and stall interplay.
If Gowin stops absorbing the regfile read into the BSRAM output register
after the bypass is removed, fall back to keeping the regfile bypass but as
a registered sel_wb2 term only (same RTL otherwise).

title: Register-file read in ID with real ID/EX operand flops and ID-stage WB bypass, so EX operand paths launch from flops not BSRAM
motivation:
The current worst path (r3s0, 21 ns, 40 cells) starts at the register-file
RAM (cpu/u_rf/regs_regs_0_0_s0, a BSRAM whose clk->out is several ns), runs

title: Registered misprediction redirect (recover from EX/MEM) plus registered one-hot operand selects, with a hashed 64-entry BHT paying back the extra cycle
motivation:
Measured on the 2K -O3 CoreMark ELF with the Python ISS (2.937M instrs, 4.203M
cycles, CPI 1.43): 532k conditional branches, 56.0k mispredicted by the 32x2
bimodal (10.5%), 13.8k returns (JALR is never predicted). At 2 bubbles each that
is only ~3.3% of runtime; an ideal infinite bimodal (39.9k) or ideal local-history
predictor (34k) would recover <=0.8%, and a RAS for the returns ~0.65%. Predictor
accuracy alone cannot clear the 4.6% bar, so the only lever left in this category
is the recovery path timing. A fresh `make timing` of the current head (r3s0)
shows a TIED wall at 15.6-15.7 ns data delay: (a) regfile BSRAM -> write-first
bypass LUT -> rs2/rs1 forward mux (3 LUTs) -> alu_a/b mux -> 32-bit compare carry
chain -> redirect -> `pc` CE / ID-EX ctrl RESET / valid (path 1-3, 5-9, 23: 6.4 ns
of the 15.7 ns is the compare->redirect->pc-mux/flush tail), and (b) the same
front end -> adder/shifter -> result mux -> EX/MEM.alu_result D (path 4, 10, 13,
14, 22: 21.009 ns vs 21.018 ns), and (c) EX/MEM.rd -> forward-select compare ->
mux -> alu_result (path 21, 15.62 ns). Cutting only the redirect tail would be
Fmax-neutral (the ALU leg is 0.01 ns behind), and every leg shares the same
5-LUT operand front end (bypass LUT + 3-LUT fwd mux + alu_a mux).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Two coupled changes that together lower the wall; neither is useful alone.
(A) Registered redirect. EX resolves branch/JALR as today but only registers the
verdict: mispred_q (EX/MEM) <= (actual_taken ^ pred_taken) && !misalign_fault &&
!redirect_m. The corrected PC is already in EX/MEM as `pc_next`, so
redirect_m = ex_mem.valid && mispred_q and target = ex_mem.pc_next, both direct
flop outputs; the EX redirect_target mux is deleted. redirect_m replaces
`redirect` in the if_stage PC mux (still priority over stall), the IF NOP mask /
pred_taken qualifier, and hazard_unit flush_if/flush_id. The wrong-path pair is C
in IF (flushed as today) and B in EX: B is squashed by reusing the ex_busy
bubble branch (`else if (ex_busy || redirect_m) reg_q <= '0; mul_q <= '0`), by
gating is_div_op with !redirect_m (divider never starts on a wrong-path divide)
and by the !redirect_m mask on B's own verdict; B can't train the BHT because
train_en needs ex_mem.valid. A mispredicted branch/JALR is never a memory op so
stall_ex_mem cannot coincide with redirect_m. Penalty becomes 3 bubbles/event
(~70k events: -1.7% iter/cycle). Pay ~1.0% back with a 64-entry bimodal indexed
by pc[7:2]^pc[13:8] (trace: 41.96k mispredicts vs 56.0k), for both the fetch pc
and the registered ex_mem.pc training index (both flop-sourced, off the
imem_data->predecode->adder path); reset stays weakly taken.

and compare legs. Remove the regfile write-first bypass LUT that sits behind the
BSRAM (reg_file.sv rs?_data mux) and instead (i) add a registered copy of the
WB write data (wb_q: 32 FF, captured every cycle) as a third forwarding source,
and (ii) pre-decode the forward selects one cycle early: when an instruction
enters ID/EX compare its raw rs1/rs2 against the producers that will be in
EX/MEM (ID/EX.rd) and MEM/WB (EX/MEM.rd) next cycle and the one now in WB
(MEM/WB.rd, source wb_q), x0/valid/reg_write qualified, and register
fwd_*_onehot {none, exmem, memwb, wbq} into ID/EX (reset/flush to none; hold with
ID/EX when stalled). EX then does a flat AND-OR select (data x3-4 + one-hot
selects = 2 LUT levels) with the alu_a is_auipc/pc and alu_b is_imm choices
folded in as extra one-hot terms, and forward_unit's rd/rs 5-bit compares leave
the EX path. Net: the BSRAM->ALU operand front end drops from ~5 to ~3 LUT
levels (~1.5-2 ns), ALU adder/shift leg and compare leg both shrink, and with (A)

wrong-path B/C never retire.

title: Launch EX operands from flops: move the register file off BSRAM onto a flop array read in ID (keeps r4s0 registered one-hot forward selects)
motivation:
The current head (r4s0, 184.34 / 77.5 MHz) has its worst path at 19.26 ns,
40 cells, launched from the register file BSRAM (cpu/u_rf/regs_regs_0_0_s)
and ending at pc (cpu/u_if/pc_1_s1) through the EX operand AND-OR, the
branch compare / rs1+imm adder and `redirect`. r4s0 already removed the
select compare/priority logic from EX, so what is left in front of every EX
leg (branch compare -> redirect -> pc, alu_a -> ALU -> EX/MEM.alu_result,
jalr_sum -> redirect_target) is the BSRAM clock-to-output itself: the
critical-path launch is ~7.6 ns for the BSRAM, whereas every other EX
source (EX/MEM, MEM/WB, wb2_q) is an ordinary flop launching several ns
earlier. The BSRAM is mapped because reg_file's read is a plain array read
with a registered address; Gowin turns that into 2 BSRAMs (bsram 6 = 4 dmem
+ 2 regfile). In the timed bench netlist io_imemData is the LFSR flop vector
(fpga/core_bench_si.sv), so a flop-array read in ID starts from a flop at
the same time as everything else and has ~10 ns to reach ID/EX.
r4s1 (regfile on flops, bsram 4 / lutram 0 / ff 1735) already gained +10%
over the r3s0 head while the old EX forward select chain (compare + priority
in EX) was still in place and set its 19.07 ns path; r4s0 has since removed
that chain, so the two fixes were never combined. They attack different
stages of the same front end (select logic vs. data launch) and so should be
additive in a way the earlier same-leg proposals were not.

title: Forward at the end of EX into real operand flops (flop regfile read in ID): EX operands launch straight from flops, no EX forward mux / alu_a / alu_b mux
motivation:
I re-ran `make timing TARGET=bench` on the r4s0 head and read core_bench.tr.
The top-25 setup paths are tied within 0.2 ns (13.73-13.93 ns data delay,
5.329 ns clock insertion, 5 ns constraint -> Fmax 71.6 MHz option 0) in TWO
families: (1) 17 paths regfile BSRAM/`fwd2.ex` -> EX forward AND-OR -> 32-bit
compare -> branch_cond/redirect (5-6 LUTs, 5.1 ns after the carry chain) ->
pc D/CE and ID/EX ctrl RESET; (2) 6 paths `reg_q.fwd2.ex` flop -> forward AND-OR
-> alu_b mux -> ALU shifter/adder/result mux (7 LUTs) -> EX/MEM.alu_result D.
Both families share the same ~6 ns operand-formation head: path 3 is
select flop `fwd2.ex` Q (fanout 32, tNET 2.4 ns) -> rs2 LUT -> rs2 LUT (fanout 6,
tNET 2.0) -> `alu_b` LUT (fanout 82) = 5.8 ns before the ALU even starts, and
path 1 spends 0.9+0.45+0.85+0.37 ns in two forward LUTs after the BSRAM DO.
That is why the previous single-leg fixes were not additive: the BSRAM launch
alone (my first idea, a flop-based regfile on top of r4s0) is worth ~0.05 ns
because the flop-launched `fwd2.ex` leg is already at 13.88 ns. Only removing
the whole head from the EX cycle shortens both families at once.

the whole head from the EX cycle shortens both families at once.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move operand selection from the start of EX to the end of the previous cycle,
so the ID/EX operand registers hold the FINAL ALU/compare operands and EX
reads them directly from flops (clk->q only):
1. reg_file.sv: explicit flop file (generate per-register enables, x0 constant 0,
   reset-to-0, (* syn_ramstyle = "registers" *)) read combinationally in ID, so
   the register value reaches the ID/EX D inputs inside the ID cycle instead of
   appearing as a BSRAM output after the ID/EX boundary (r4s1 showed this
   mapping is formal/cosim-clean: ~+1.3K LUT4, +1K FF, within the 10K budget).
2. id_stage: ID/EX gets `op1`/`op2` flops. D = AND-OR of terms with a one-hot
   select computed combinationally in ID (the existing fwd_select compares, now
   unregistered; priority youngest-first):
     ex-now  : this cycle's EX result `early_masked` (ex_stage output; the late
               term, 1 LUT level before the flop: AND with sel_ex | pre-combined
               other terms),
     mem-now : load_data (new mem_stage output, comb from dmem BSRAM + align) for
               a load, else EX/MEM.alu_result|mul_q (flops),
     wb-now  : wb_w_data (replaces wb2_q),
     regfile : regs[raw_rs] (x0 -> 0).
   The ALU operand muxes are folded in: op1 = is_auipc ? in.pc : fwd(rs1);
   op2 = (alu_src && !mem_write) ? imm : fwd(rs2) (stores keep rs2 as store data;
   their address and branch targets use the dedicated rs1+imm / pc+imm adders
   which read in.imm, so the ALU result of stores/branches is never used).
   EX therefore has NO forward AND-OR, no alu_a/alu_b mux, no select flops and no
   wb2_q: rs1 = in.op1, rs2 = in.op2 feed the ALU, compare, jalr_sum adder,
   divider and store-data directly.
3. RVFI-only copies: keep `rv1`/`rv2` (pure forwarded register values, same
   AND-OR without the imm/pc terms) in ID/EX and carry them to EX/MEM rs?_val so
   rs1_rdata/rs2_rdata stay the true register values for riscv-formal's reg
   check. This logic only feeds RVFI and is pruned from the timed netlist.
4. Late producers: a result that cannot be forwarded at the end of EX without
   putting a late source on the operand D (DSP product for MUL/MULH*, the
   jump link / misalign-trap-qualified reg_write of JAL/JALR, loads) makes the
   consumer wait one cycle, exactly like load-use today: add ctrl.late_res
   (= mem_read | is_jump | alu_op in MUL*) in id_stage and generalize
   hazard_unit's load_use_hazard to `id_ex.late_res`. The consumer then captures
   the value from the MEM-now term (flops, or load_data for loads). The late
   misalign_jump term thus leaves the select cone (ex_we = reg_write for
   non-late producers), and the DSP product keeps its private mul_q flop path.
   CPI cost: MUL-use and JAL-use stalls only (<=~1% of cycles; IPC otherwise
   identical, branch/redirect/divider/stall behaviour unchanged).
Expected timing: ALU leg = op flop -> (net ~2 ns for the fanout) -> ALU 7 levels ->
early_masked -> 1 operand-D LUT: ~11.3 ns vs 13.9 ns today; compare leg = op flop
-> carry chain -> 5.1 ns tail: ~10.7 ns vs 13.9 ns; ID-cycle legs (regfile 32:1 mux
or select compare -> AND-OR -> D, BSRAM-aligned load_data -> AND-OR -> D) ~8-10 ns.
New wall ~11-11.5 ns (Fmax ~87-90 MHz vs 77.5), net of ~1% IPC loss about +15%.

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-002-r5s1 (improvement, +18.66%): Resolving forwarding, the AUIPC pc and the ALU immediate at the end of ID (ID/EX `op1`/`op2` flops fed by a one-hot AND-OR of EX-now `early_masked`, MEM-now/`load_data`, WB-now and a flop regfile read; RVFI-only `rv1`/`rv2` copies kept for riscv-formal) beat the r4s0 head 184.34 -> 218.74 (above the predicted +15%) because both worst-path families shared the ~6 ns EX operand head (select flop fanout 32 -> forward LUTs -> `alu_b` mux fanout 82), so only removing that head from EX shortened both the compare->`redirect` and ALU->EX/MEM legs at once, and it stayed cheap in CPI by marking producers that can't forward at end of EX (loads, JAL/JALR link, MUL* DSP product) with `ctrl.late_res` and stalling only their immediate consumer like load-use — when a mux sits on every EX leg, move it across the pipeline register and pay for the few late producers with a one-cycle consumer stall rather than putting them on the operand D inputs.

title: Fetch-directed prediction queue: BHT/JAL predictor runs ahead into a 2-entry (pc, instr, pred_taken) queue so non-imem stalls no longer waste imem slots
motivation:
Predictor accuracy alone is exhausted on this core. r4s2's ISS trace of the
2K -O3 CoreMark ELF (2.937M instrs, 4.203M cycles, CPI 1.43) gives 56k
mispredicts of 532k conditional branches (10.5%) plus 13.8k returns: at a
1-2 cycle penalty that is <=3.3% of runtime, and an ideal direction
predictor or a RAS recovers <1% each. Re-timing the recovery path (a
registered redirect) is Fmax-neutral while the ALU->EX/MEM.alu_result leg
ties the compare->redirect->pc leg (r4s2 was broken for that reason and
because it bundled two changes). So the remaining lever that keeps the
predictor in the loop is the *fetch* side: the CPI floor set by the 22%
imem stall is 1/0.78 = 1.28 (3.77M cycles) vs 1.43 measured, a 10% gap.
Most of that gap is slots the imem delivered but the pipeline could not take:
today the PC register and the combinational IF/ID bundle hold whenever
stall_if = load_use | dmem_stall | ex_busy, so an instruction that imem
returned in a dmem-stall / load-use / divide cycle (ready=1 in 78% of
them) is thrown away and re-fetched later, and the prediction made for it
is thrown away with it. ~0.34M cycles (8%) of the run are such non-imem
stall cycles, ~0.27M of them with imem_ready=1. A small queue between the
predicting fetch stage and ID banks those words, so later random imem
misses (22% of cycles) are covered by buffered instructions instead of
bubbles. Simple occupancy model (fill rate ~6%/cycle when empty, drain by an
imem miss ~22%/cycle): a 1-entry buffer recovers ~0.19M cycles (+4.5%), a
2-entry buffer ~0.25M (+6%). All the new logic is on the fetch/ID side; the
timed critical legs (regfile BSRAM -> forward AND-OR -> compare/ALU ->
redirect/pc, EX/MEM.alu_result) are untouched, and imem_data is a flop
(LFSR) in the timed netlist so one extra LUT in front of the decoder is
off the critical path.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Turn if_stage into a fetch-directed front end: the existing predictor
(predecode of the raw word, 32x2 bimodal BHT, JAL always-taken, adder for
pc+imm, never-predict-misaligned / JALR) keeps running at the FETCH pc
exactly as today, but its result is pushed into a small queue instead of
being consumed only if ID happens to be ready that cycle.

Queue: DEPTH=2 entries of {pc[31:2], instr[31:0], pred_taken}, shift-register
style (head = entry 0), q_cnt in {0,1,2}, cleared by reset and by `redirect`.
`cur` = the instruction ID looks at this cycle = (q_cnt != 0) ? head : the
word on io_imemData (with the predecode pred_taken/pc of the fetch address).
  cur_valid = (q_cnt != 0) || io_imemReady
ID decodes cur_instr (replaces io_imemData for raw_instr, raw_rs1/rs2 and the
hazard unit's if_id_rs1/rs2); `in.pc` / `in.pred_taken` come from the head
entry or the fetch pc / predecode.

Control (hazard_unit + if_stage), with load_use computed from cur_instr:
  id_stall   = dmem_stall || load_use || ex_busy                (unchanged)
  consume    = cur_valid && !id_stall && !redirect  (ID/EX captures cur, valid=1)
  flush_id   = (load_use || redirect || !cur_valid) && !dmem_stall && !ex_busy
               (unchanged form; `!cur_valid` replaces `imem_stall`)
  accept     = io_imemReady && !redirect && (q_cnt != DEPTH || consume)
               -> the fetched word is taken: pc <= pred_taken ? pred_target : pc+4
               and it goes straight to ID if q_cnt==0 && consume, otherwise it is
               enqueued (after a simultaneous dequeue of the head if consume).
  redirect   : unchanged priority over everything: pc <= redirect_target,
               q_cnt <= 0, ID/EX bubble, so wrong-path words in the queue and
               the fetched word are all dropped (all of them are younger than the
               redirecting EX instruction).
stall_if is replaced by `accept` as the PC enable. A load-use bubble no longer
forces a refetch: the consumer stays at the head of the queue (or is
enqueued) and is re-presented next cycle; a dmem/divide stall keeps filling
the queue until full, then holds the PC.
pred_taken travels with the entry and is captured into ID/EX only when the
entry is consumed (ID/EX.pred_taken <= cur_pred && valid, cleared by flush as
today), so EX's `redirect = actual_taken ^ pred_taken` logic, redirect_target
keyed on the registered pred_taken, and BHT training from EX/MEM are all
unchanged. io_imemAddr stays = pc (the fetch address), so imem_data -> predecode
-> adder -> pc loop is unchanged, plus one mux level (cur select) in front of
the decoder/regfile address/hazard compare.

RVFI/formal: instructions still enter ID/EX strictly in program order with
their own pc, so pc_fwd, order and liveness are preserved (every cycle with
imem ready and queue space makes progress). Memory-bus bounds are unchanged
(fetch addresses are the same set as before, never a speculative new one).
If depth-2 timing is bad, fall back to DEPTH=1 (head/tail merge, ~+4.5%).
Not included on purpose: BHT re-hash / RAS (each <1%), registered redirect.

title: Late-select EX tail: one LUT after each carry chain (compare -> redirect cofactor mux, adder -> one-hot result OR) plus a private compare operand copy
motivation:
I re-ran `make timing TARGET=bench` on the r5s1 head and read core_bench.tr
(place option 0, 10.23 ns data delay, constraint 5 ns). 21 of the top-25
setup paths are two EX legs that both start at ID/EX op1/op2 flops and both
spend their time AFTER the 32-bit carry chain, not in it:
(1) op2_0 (fanout 81, net 2.58 ns) -> shared compare/SUB carry chain
    (32 cells x 0.035 = 1.1 ns) -> n1494_s6 -> n1494_s3 (branch_cond mux)
    -> redirect_Z_s2 -> _s1 -> _s (5 LUT levels, 4.0 ns incl. nets, the
    last with fanout 36) -> then either pc CE/D (+2 LUTs: u_if n395/
    pc_31_s3, net 1.2 + 0.8 ns) or ID/EX ctrl/valid RESET (+3 LUTs:
    u_if n395_s5 -> u_id n898_s2 -> n898_s0 fanout 20, 3.2 ns). Arrival
    15.55 ns; the carry chain output is at 9.2 ns, so 6.3 ns (62% of
    the data delay) is post-chain redirect/flush decoding.
(2) op2_4 (fanout 67, net 2.3 ns) -> adder chain -> SUM at 9.58 ns ->
    4 LUT levels (alu case(op) mux, alt_sel/jump mux, early_masked mask)
    -> EX/MEM.alu_result D at 15.55 ns: 6 ns of mux tail behind the adder.
The mapper treats the carry-chain output like any other input (unit
depth), but it arrives ~3.5 ns after every other term feeding the same
mux, so the late signal ends up at the DEEPEST point of the mux cone
instead of the last LUT. The other three near-critical families
(imem -> fwd compare -> op1 D, BSRAM DO -> load align -> op2 D, imem ->
pred adder -> pc D) are only 0.02-0.05 ns less critical, so this is a
balanced wall, but F1 + F2 are the families with the largest removable
slack (>= 2 LUT levels each) and they own the endpoints with the highest
fanout (pc CE 30, ID/EX reset 20-35).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make the carry-chain results the LAST select of every cone they feed.
All other terms are computed from flops in parallel (they are available
~3 ns earlier than the chain output) and merged with the late signal in a
single LUT. No architectural/IPC change (cycle count must stay 4240287).

1. ex_stage.sv, compare: replace the 6-way case with one unified compare.
   lt = ($unsigned({rs1[31]^sgn, rs1[30:0]}) < $unsigned({rs2[31]^sgn,
   rs2[30:0]})) with sgn = !branch_op[1] (the flip sits on the MSB cell at
   the end of the chain, operands are flops), eq = (rs1 == rs2), and
   branch_cond = branch_op[0] ^ (branch_op[2] ? lt : eq)  (funct3
   encoding: BEQ 000, BNE 001, BLT 100, BGE 101, BLTU 110, BGEU 111;
   non-branches are masked by is_branch). One chain instead of the
   signed+unsigned pair currently merged into the SUB chain.
2. ex_stage.sv, redirect: Shannon-expand on the single late bit
   branch_cond. Precompute from flops/low adder bits
      R1 = ((is_branch | is_jump) ^ pred_taken) & !((is_branch & bt_mis) | jmp_mis)
      R0 = (is_jump ^ pred_taken) & !jmp_mis
   with bt_mis = branch_target[1:0] != 0 and jmp_mis = is_jump &&
   jump_target[1:0] != 0 (both from the low 2 bits of the pc+imm / rs1+imm
   adders: early), and write `redirect = branch_cond ? R1 : R0`. Likewise
   export `misalign_fault` for the EX/MEM ctrl_with_trap / pc_next path as
   `branch_cond ? M1 : M0` instead of the current late branch_taken AND.
   Keep R1/R0/M1/M0 as separate named nets with `(* keep *)` so the mapper
   does not fold the late bit back into the middle of the cone.
3. Consumers of `redirect` take it as the last mux select too:
     - if_stage pc: D = redirect ? redirect_target : next_pc (already a
       mux; make CE = redirect | !stall a single LUT of redirect and one
       precomputed early `!stall`), and out.valid / pred_taken masks use the
       same form;
     - hazard_unit / id_stage ID/EX ctrl+valid+pred_taken reset:
       sr = redirect ? (reset | !hold) : (reset | early_flush & !hold)
       with hold = dmem_stall | ex_busy and early_flush = load_use |
       imem_stall (all flop/LFSR derived), i.e. ONE LUT between `redirect`
       and the 20-35 RESET pins instead of u_if n395 -> n898_s2 -> n898_s0.
   Net effect: post-chain depth for the redirect legs goes from 5 + 2..3 LUT
   levels to 1 (cond) + 1 (redirect) + 1 (consumer select) ~ 3 levels.
4. alu.sv / ex_stage.sv, adder leg: express alu_fast/early_masked as a
   one-hot AND-OR whose adder term is the only late input:
      early_masked[i] = (sel_addsub & sum[i]) | other[i]
   where sel_addsub is an early decode of ALU_ADD/ALU_SUB (also true for
   the LOAD/STORE/branch ADD encodings that do not matter) and other[i]
   collects logic ops, slt/sltu (1 bit), shifter output, LUI, PC+4 (jump),
   divider result and the mul mask, all selected by early one-hot decodes
   of alu_op (registered ID/EX ctrl -> 1-2 LUTs, off the chain). The SUM
   bit then needs exactly one LUT before alu_result D (and one more
   before the ID-stage ex-now forward AND-OR, which is the existing
   last LUT). Use a single ADD/SUB chain with an XOR-conditioned b
   (sub = alu_op == ALU_SUB) and keep the SLT/SLTU result on the shared
   compare chain's lt output rather than a second subtractor.
5. Fanout split on the compare/redirect leg (id_stage.sv + core_pkg.sv):
   add private copies cmp1/cmp2 of the final operands to ID/EX (same D

title: Registered redirect with squash-in-EX: branch compare ends at one flop, wrong-path op is killed by redir_q
motivation:
After r5s1 (head 218.74, 92.75 MHz median, best seed 97.5) the worst path is
cpu/u_id/reg_q.op2_0 -> 32-bit compare carry chain in ex_stage -> branch_cond
-> `redirect` -> flush_id -> ID/EX ctrl RESET (reg_q.ctrl.is_jalr), 37 cells,
arrival 15.555 ns incl. 5.33 ns clock insertion, i.e. ~10.2 ns of data delay.
`redirect` is a very late 1-bit signal (end of the carry chain) that fans out
to ~30 ID/EX ctrl reset pins, the pc mux/CE (32 flops) and the IF/ID valid and
pred_taken masks. In-cycle fixes of that cone (r2s0: take redirect off the
NOP-mask cone) were real but bounded gains; r4s2 tried a registered redirect
but bundled it with a second change and was broken. r5s2's analysis shows
redirect events are rare: ~56k mispredicts + 13.8k JALR returns over 4.2M
cycles (~1.7% of cycles), so adding one cycle to recovery costs ~1.7% IPC but
removes the whole compare->redirect->{flush, pc, valid} fanout tail from the
timed cycle (the compare then ends at a single D pin).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make the EX redirect a registered event and kill the one wrong-path
instruction in EX instead of at ID capture. Only ex_stage.sv and the core.sv
wiring change; id_stage, hazard_unit and if_stage keep their ports and logic
(they simply see a flop-driven `redirect`).

ex_stage: compute redirect_raw = (actual_taken ^ in.pred_taken) &&
!misalign_fault && !redir_q && !stall (stall = dmem stall: the branch has not
left EX yet, it retries when it advances). Register
  redir_q     <= redirect_raw
  redir_tgt_q <= redirect_target (32 flops, no CE needed; only consumed when
                                  redir_q is 1)
`redirect_target` is a mux keyed on registered pred_taken / is_jump / is_jalr
of early adders (pc+4, pc+imm, rs1+imm), so only the 1-bit select is late.
The ex_stage outputs `redirect` / `redirect_target` become redir_q /
redir_tgt_q; core.sv keeps wiring them to if_stage and hazard_unit unchanged.
Reset clears redir_q.

Cycle behaviour. Cycle t: mispredicted branch X in EX, wrong-path A in ID
(captured into ID/EX as valid, nobody flushes it yet), redir_q <= 1.
Cycle t+1: X is in MEM, A in EX, B in ID/fetch, redir_q = 1:
  - B is flushed (flush_id / flush_if from the flop) and pc <= redir_tgt_q,
    identical to today's recovery except the signal now comes from flops;
  - A is squashed in EX: the existing `else if (ex_busy)` bubble branch of the
    EX/MEM register (and of mul_q) becomes `else if (ex_busy || redir_q)` so
    EX/MEM takes valid=0/ctrl=0 and A never retires, writes a register,
    touches dmem, trains the BHT or forwards (the ctrl is zero from MEM on);
    the ex-now forward term feeds only B, which is flushed anyway, so
    id_stage needs no change;
  - redirect_raw is gated by !redir_q so A (a wrong-path branch/JALR) cannot
    redirect, and is_div_op = in.valid && !redir_q && div-op so a wrong-path
    divide never starts the divider or raises ex_busy (which would suppress
    flush_id);
  - A as a late producer may raise load_use_hazard against B; that only holds
    PC/ID, and the redirect already has priority over stall in if_stage and
    over stall_id in id_stage (flush wins), so no extra gating is needed.
Cycle t+2: pc = target, EX holds the bubble from B's flush, redir_q = 0.
dmem_stall cannot coincide with redir_q because the only instruction in MEM
at t+1 is the (non-memory) branch/jump, and the branch's own EX->MEM move is
what arms redir_q (redirect_raw is gated by !stall).

Compatibility: rvfi_order, pc_next (X keeps the correct resolved pc_next in
EX/MEM), pc_fwd, the BHT training from EX/MEM, JALR-always-redirects and the
misaligned-target trap (redirect suppressed, linear PC) are unchanged. The
only visible change is a 2-cycle (was 1) bubble per EX redirect.

Expected: the compare->redirect fanout tail (the ~3-4 ns of LUT levels and
high-fanout nets after the carry chain) leaves the timed cycle; the other
legs (ALU -> early_masked -> operand D, dmem BSRAM -> load_data -> operand D)
are expected within ~1 ns of the current worst, so the median period should
fall from ~10.8 ns toward ~9.8-10.0 ns (+8-10% Fmax) for ~1.7% more cycles,
net about +6%. Risks: formal pc/liveness consistency of the squash, and the
next-worst leg (ALU/BSRAM) absorbing most of the gain.

changes.description: Register the redirect: redirect_raw (gated by !redir_q, !stall, !misalign_fault) -> redir_q flop + redir_tgt_q flops, exported as redirect/redirect_target; squash the EX op while redir_q (EX/MEM and mul_q take bubbles via `ex_busy || redir_q`, is_div_op gated by !redir_q).
Keep wiring redirect/redirect_target (now flop outputs of ex_stage) to if_stage and hazard_unit; no port changes. Update comments.

Register the redirect: redirect_raw (gated by !redir_q, !stall, !misalign_fault) -> redir_q flop + redir_tgt_q flops, exported as redirect/redirect_target; squash the EX op while redir_q (EX/MEM and mul_q take bubbles via `ex_busy || redir_q`, is_div_op gated by !redir_q).
Keep wiring redirect/redirect_target (now flop outputs of ex_stage) to if_stage and hazard_unit; no port changes. Update comments.

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-002-r6s1 (improvement, +5.28%): Registering the EX `redirect`/`redirect_target` (`redir_q`/`redir_tgt_q`, branch compare now ends at one D pin) and squashing the single wrong-path op in EX the next cycle by reusing the existing `ex_busy` bubble arm (`else if (ex_busy || redir_q)` on EX/MEM and `mul_q`) took fitness 218.74 -> 230.30, roughly the predicted +6% net of a ~1.7% IPC cost (2-cycle instead of 1-cycle mispredict/JALR bubble), because redirects are rare (~70k per 4.2M cycles) so an extra recovery cycle is far cheaper than the compare -> redirect -> {flush_id, pc mux/CE, IF/ID masks} fanout tail it removes from the timed cycle — a rare, very late 1-bit control event is better registered with the already-advanced younger op squashed one stage later (and gated with `!redir_q` from starting side effects such as a divide or a second redirect) than fixed with in-cycle logic, though the implied Fmax gain (~+7%) fell short of the +8-10% hoped for since the ALU/BSRAM legs sit just behind it.

title: Redirect-independent 2-entry fetch skid queue behind the predicting fetch stage (bank imem words delivered during load-use/dmem/divide stalls)
motivation:
Predictor accuracy is exhausted on this core: r4s2's ISS trace of the 2K -O3
CoreMark ELF (2.937M instrs) shows 56k mispredicts of 532k conditional
branches (10.5%) plus 13.8k returns, i.e. <=3.3% of runtime at a 1-2 cycle
penalty, and an ideal direction predictor or a RAS each recover <1%. The
largest CPI term still attached to the predicting fetch stage is imem slots
that are *delivered but thrown away*: the PC register and the combinational
IF/ID bundle simply hold when stall_if = load_use | dmem_stall | ex_busy, so a
word the imem returned in such a cycle (ready=1 in 78% of them) is dropped,
re-fetched later, and exposed again to the 22% random imem miss (together with
the BHT/JAL prediction made for it). The current CPI is ~1.44 (4.24M cycles /
2.937M instrs) against an imem-only floor of 1/0.78 = 1.28; ~0.27M cycles of
the run are consumer-stall cycles with imem_ready=1. r5s2 banked those words
in a 2-entry queue and measured 3.99M vs 4.20M cycles (-5.0%, i.e. +5.3%
iter/cycle) but lost 10.5% Fmax (77.5 -> 69.4 MHz). Its change description
says the queue was "cleared by reset/redirect" with a PC enable of
accept = imem_ready && (q_cnt != DEPTH || consume) && !redirect, and its
reported worst path ends in u_if pc (BSRAM regfile -> ... -> u_if, 10 cells,
19.8 ns). My reading (inferred from that description and path, NOT measured
separately) is that putting `redirect` on the queue slots' load enables and
on q_cnt gave the late redirect net a much larger fan-out (~140 queue flops
plus PC). The worst path of the current head (15.555 ns, module list
u_ex/u_alu -> u_ex -> u_if -> u_id) looks like the same compare -> redirect ->
u_if/u_id family, so any extra redirect load is expected to cost Fmax again.
The idea is sound; the implementation structure is what is being changed.
This hypothesis keeps the CPI gain and fixes the timing structure.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a small fetch skid queue (DEPTH=2: q[0] = head/oldest, q[1]) INSIDE
if_stage, between the predicting fetch (imem word + BHT/JAL predecode at `pc`)
and the ID cone, with these timing rules (the point of the proposal):

1. `redirect` may only touch (a) the existing pc-register mux (priority over
   everything, unchanged), (b) the existing `out.valid` / `flush_id` terms and
   (c) the TWO occupancy flops (cnt <= 0). Queue DATA flops (instr[31:0],
   pc[31:2], pred_taken) load on a redirect-free enable: they simply capture
   the fetch word whenever the queue is not holding (no reset, no clear on
   redirect: stale data is dead once cnt=0). Net added redirect fan-out: ~2
   flops instead of ~140.
2. The accept / consume terms are functions of FLOPS only:
     consume = !stall_id            (stall_id = dmem_stall | load_use | ex_busy;
                                     dmem_ready/ex_mem op, id_ex rd/late_res,
                                     divider state, and the presented word's
                                     rs1/rs2 -- all flop- or LFSR-driven)
     accept  = imem_ready && (cnt != DEPTH || consume)
   pc <= redirect ? redirect_target : (accept ? next_pc : pc)  -- identical
   shape to today's `!stall` enable, with `accept` replacing `!stall_if`.
   `stall_if` (the old PC-hold OR) is deleted from hazard_unit's PC path.
3. Presented word P = (cnt != 0) ? q[0] : fetch word (imem_data, pc,
   pred_taken). P feeds exactly what imem_data feeds today: the decoder,
   imm_gen, regfile read addresses, fwd_select compares, hazard load-use
   compare, and ID/EX pc/instr/valid/pred_taken. In the timed netlist
   imem_data is a flop (LFSR), so the 2:1 mux (1 LUT) sits in front of the
   decoder / regfile-read / fwd_select cones. ASSUMPTION (not measured here):
   those cones are shorter than the 15.5 ns EX compare -> redirect leg; the
   implementer should check `make timing` for the P-mux -> regfile read ->
   forward AND-OR -> op1_d leg and, if it is within ~1 ns of the wall, drop
   the mux from the regfile-address cone by keeping regfile reads on the
   fetch word and re-reading from the queue only when cnt != 0.
4. Occupancy: pop = (cnt != 0) && consume; push = accept && !(cnt == 0 &&
   consume) (a word consumed straight from the fetch bypass never enters the
   queue); cnt_next = redirect ? 0 : cnt - pop + push. When cnt == DEPTH and
   consume, the head is popped and the fetch word shifts in the same cycle.
5. Bubble generation moves from `imem_stall` to `!p_valid`, with
   p_valid = (cnt != 0) || imem_ready: with a non-empty queue an imem miss no
   longer injects an ID/EX bubble (this is where the cycles are recovered).
   hazard_unit: flush_if = redirect || !p_valid; flush_id =
   (load_use || redirect || !p_valid) && !dmem_stall && !ex_busy; stall_id
   unchanged; load_use uses P's rs1/rs2 (new input from if_stage's presented
   raw word instead of io_imemData).
6. pred_taken is recorded per word at the moment the PC is steered by it
   (stored in the queue slot) and travels with P: out.pred_taken =
   P.pred_taken && p_valid && !redirect. EX still redirects only on
   actual_taken ^ pred_taken and keys redirect_target on the registered
   pred_taken, so ex_stage.sv is untouched. BHT read/training and the
   predecode adder are unchanged (they still operate on the *fetch* word at
   `pc`, one entry ahead of ID).
7. Mispredict penalty is unchanged (redirect empties the queue, the target is
   fetched next cycle and bypasses straight into ID).

Expected effect: +~5% iter/cycle from r5s2's measured -5.0% cycles
(4.20M -> 3.99M at the r4s0 head; the current head's ~4.24M, derived from
fitness / Fmax, should behave similarly), at Fmax parity IF the redirect
tail gains no fan-out and no new LUT level (by construction here: only the
2 cnt flops are added to it). Fmax parity is the main risk: +5% is only just
above the 4.6% acceptance bar, so any Fmax loss or unlucky P&R sinks it. If timing allows, a DEPTH=3 parameter would
recover a further ~1%, but start at DEPTH=2.

Correctness checks the implementer must keep: formal (rvfi order/pc_fwd rely
on P.pc matching the instruction actually retired, and on redirect killing
every queued wrong-path word incl. while dmem_stall holds the branch in
ID/EX and redirect re-fires each stall cycle); cosim with istall/dstall
(queue + redirect + dmem stall + divide stall interleavings); misaligned
branch/JAL targets must still never be predicted (unchanged predecode check).

title: Single-LUT EX result tail: jump link through the ALU adder, div/mul as pure OR terms, registered one-hot result class
motivation:
After r6s1 the registered redirect removed the compare -> redirect fan-out, and the worst
path is now the remaining EX leg: ID/EX op2 flop (fanout ~80) -> 32-bit add carry chain ->
alu case(op) mux -> alt_sel (JAL/JALR pc+4 / divider result) mux -> early_masked mul mask ->
EX/MEM.alu_result D (and, one LUT later, the end-of-EX forward into the ID/EX op1/op2 D pins).
Per the r6s0 report the chain output is ready ~3.5 ns after every other term of that cone,
yet it sits at the DEEPEST point of a 4-LUT mux tail (~6 ns of the ~10 ns data delay).
Three of those tail legs are logically redundant: (1) JAL/JALR link = pc+4 can be produced by
the ALU ADD itself if ID hands it op1=pc, op2=4 (ID already muxes the AUIPC pc into op1);
(2) the divider/multiplier ops already read 0 on the ALU's fast_out leg, so the divide result
can be merged with a plain OR instead of an alt_sel mux and the `early_masked` mul mask is a
no-op; (3) the add/sub select can be a registered one-hot bit instead of an op[4:0] decode
behind the carry chain. r6s0 tried a similar late-select tail but bundled it with the
compare/redirect cone (not additive) and a +64 FF operand copy; the redirect leg is now gone.

hypothesis.motivation:
After r6s1 the registered redirect removed the compare -> redirect fan-out, and the worst
path is now the remaining EX leg: ID/EX op2 flop (fanout ~80) -> 32-bit add carry chain ->
alu case(op) mux -> alt_sel (JAL/JALR pc+4 / divider result) mux -> early_masked mul mask ->
EX/MEM.alu_result D (and, one LUT later, the end-of-EX forward into the ID/EX op1/op2 D pins).
Per the r6s0 report the chain output is ready ~3.5 ns after every other term of that cone,
yet it sits at the DEEPEST point of a 4-LUT mux tail (~6 ns of the ~10 ns data delay).
Three of those tail legs are logically redundant: (1) JAL/JALR link = pc+4 can be produced by
the ALU ADD itself if ID hands it op1=pc, op2=4 (ID already muxes the AUIPC pc into op1);
(2) the divider/multiplier ops already read 0 on the ALU's fast_out leg, so the divide result
can be merged with a plain OR instead of an alt_sel mux and the `early_masked` mul mask is a
no-op; (3) the add/sub select can be a registered one-hot bit instead of an op[4:0] decode
behind the carry chain. r6s0 tried a similar late-select tail but bundled it with the
compare/redirect cone (not additive) and a +64 FF operand copy; the redirect leg is now gone.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make the carry-chain output the LAST select of the EX result cone, with no architectural or
CPI change (cycle count must stay 4309869).

1. id_stage.sv / imm_gen.sv: for JAL/JALR, ID/EX op1 = in.pc (extend `use_pc` to
   is_auipc || is_jump) and op2 = 32'd4 (new imm_gen output `imm_alu`, = 4 for JAL/JALR and
   `imm` otherwise; `imm` itself still goes to the ID/EX imm register for the pc+imm target).
   JAL/JALR keep alu_op = ALU_ADD and late_res = 1 (consumer stall unchanged: the link's
   reg_write is still trap-qualified in EX).
2. ex_stage.sv: jalr_sum (also the load/store mem_addr) becomes in.rv1 + in.imm (rv1 is the
   pure forwarded rs1, identical to op1 for every non-AUIPC/non-jump op). Delete the
   `in.ctrl.is_jump ? pc+4 : div_result` alt mux. Replace
   early_masked = (mul ? 0 : (alt_sel ? alt_result : alu_fast)) by
   early_masked = alu_fast | (div_result & {32{is_div_op}}) -- valid because the ALU's fast_out
   is 0 for every MUL*/DIV*/REM* op (HW_DIV = 0) and the div term is an early flop-derived AND.
3. alu.sv: build fast_out as `({32{sel_addsub}} & sum) | other` where
   sum = a + (b ^ {32{sub}}) + sub is ONE add/sub chain (ALU_ADD/ALU_SUB) and `other` is the
   OR of the logic / shift / SLT / SLTU / LUI legs, each gated by registered one-hot class bits
   decoded in ID and carried in ctrl_t (sel_addsub, sub; core_pkg.sv). All `other` terms come
   from flops in parallel with the chain, so the tail after the chain is one LUT (sum bit,
   sel_addsub, other bit). Bit 0 combines the SLT/SLTU result (also a chain-end signal) in a
   2-input LUT after a precombined early term. Keep the RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS branch and the
   `out` (full result) port behaviour for test_alu.py unchanged (the new class bits default
   from `op` inside alu.sv so the standalone ALU test still passes).
4. Optional if timing shows it is also tied: precompute the load-align one-hot byte-lane /
   sign-extend selects as flops next to the EX/MEM mem_addr flop so mem_ld_val is a one-level
   AND-OR of dmem_rdata (BSRAM DO -> op D leg).

Expected effect: the post-chain tail drops from ~4 LUT levels to 1 and the forward leg into
op1/op2 D loses the same 3 levels, taking ~2-3 ns off the EX ALU family; the other families
(imem -> fwd compare -> op D, load align -> op D, predecode -> pc D) are not touched, so the
realised Fmax gain is bounded by whichever of those is next (expected net ~+5%).

title: Compare-class result leg (SLT/SLTU) leaves the EX result mux: 1-bit cmp_q flop merged post-register like mul_q, one shared lt/ltu chain
motivation:
The head's recorded worst path (r6s1 log) is ID/EX op2_0 -> a full 32-bit carry
chain (37 cells, 12 logic levels) -> EX/MEM alu_result_0. The endpoint is bit 0,
and the only ALU leg whose bit 0 depends on the top of a carry chain is SLT/SLTU
(add/sub/logic bit 0 does not). So the deepest path in the core is the compare
chain followed by the ALU case mux, the alt_sel (jump/divide) mux and the
early_masked mask before the flop; the same early_masked also feeds the EX-now
forward term in ID, so every long tail on this leg is paid twice. r6s0's
late-select rewrite tried to fix this with LUT-level cofactor tricks and
failed because it left the compare on the shared result mux; r3s0 showed the
winning move for a late unit is to take it off the shared mux and merge it
AFTER the register (mul_q). SLT/SLTU is the other late leg and is rare in the
CoreMark timed region (a few percent of instructions, and most consumers are
branches/ANDs a cycle or more later).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make SLT/SLTU/SLTI/SLTIU a second "late result" class next to MUL*:
  1. alu.sv: compute lt (signed) and ltu once and export them as outputs. The
     combinational `out` port (used by test_alu.py) still returns the full
     SLT/SLTU result, but `fast_out` returns 0 for SLT/SLTU, so the compare
     chain no longer feeds fast_out / early_result / early_masked / the ID
     EX-now forward AND-OR.
  2. ex_stage.sv: add a 1-bit flop cmp_q with D = (alu_op==ALU_SLTU) ? ltu :
     (alu_op==ALU_SLT) ? lt : 0, bubble/stall gated exactly like mul_q
     (reset -> 0, stall -> hold, ex_busy || redir_q -> 0). EX/MEM.alu_result
     becomes reg_q.alu_result | mul_q | {31'b0, cmp_q} (a one-LUT OR on
     bit 0 only, on the EX/MEM forwarding leg that launches from a flop and
     already hides the mul_q OR). The branch comparator (BLT/BGE/BLTU/BGEU)
     reads the same lt/ltu wires instead of its own `<`/`>=` expressions, so
     there is one compare chain for the whole EX stage (fewer chains hanging
     off the op1/op2 flops, lower fanout on op2); BEQ/BNE keep the XOR-reduce.
     The compare chain's sinks are then only the cmp_q D pin (chain -> 1 LUT)
     and the already-registered redirect (redir_q) logic.
  3. id_stage.sv: add ALU_SLT/ALU_SLTU to ctrl.late_res. The existing
     hazard_unit load-use mechanism then stalls the immediate consumer one
     cycle (ex_we is already gated by !late_res, so there is no EX-now
     forward from SLT), and the consumer takes the value from the MEM-now
     term (mem_alu_val = EX/MEM.alu_result, which now includes cmp_q).
Result: the deepest tail on the compare leg (chain + ~4 LUT levels) shrinks
to chain + 1 LUT, and the compare chain's fanout drops. Cost is one consumer
bubble on SLT/SLTU -> immediately-dependent instruction, estimated ~1% iter/
cycle (cycles 4.31M -> ~4.35M). Expected Fmax gain needs the adder->alu_result
leg and the other families listed in LESSONS (r6s0) to sit a little behind
the compare leg, which the r6s1 report suggests (the compare leg was the single
worst path after the redirect was registered); implementer should run
`make timing TARGET=bench` and report the new worst path.

title: Flop-top return-address stack: predict `ret` (jalr x0,0(ra)) at fetch, verify with a 31-bit rs1 equality in EX
motivation:
A CoreMark trace of the timed region (ISS over the 2K/-O3 ELF, 2.92M instrs,
4.31M cycles) shows where redirect cycles come from. Conditional branches:
529,588, of which the 32-entry bimodal BHT mispredicts 55.5k (33k are far-forward
data-dependent, 18.8k are loop exits; short forward "hammocks" are only 4.7k, so
predication is not worth building). JALR: 13,735, ALL of them `ret`
(jalr x0,0(x1)), and IF never predicts JALR, so every one takes the full 2-bubble
registered redirect. A 4-deep return stack mispredicts only 12 of those 13,735
returns; bimodal-256/1024 would save 11k/16k mispredicts and gshare-1024/h10
17k, but those need big flop/LUT-RAM tables in the fetch cone for <=0.8%.
Total redirect cost today is ~69.3k x 2 = 139k cycles = 3.2% of the run, so a
predictor can never gain more than ~3.2%; RAS is the only piece that is
near-perfect (>99.9%) and cheap, worth 27.5k cycles (~0.64%). Honest bound: this
is a small, nearly timing-neutral IPC change, the best single predictor angle
left after the BHT/JAL predictor and the registered redirect already landed.
