hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a 4-entry shift-register return-address stack in if_stage whose top entry
`ras_q[0]` is a plain flop (no pointer mux, so ras top -> pc D adds no logic on
the fetch path). Maintenance is retire-side, like the BHT training: from the
EX/MEM register, a valid non-illegal JAL/JALR with rd==x1 (or x5) pushes
ex_mem.pc+4 (shift down), a valid JALR with rd==x0, rs1==x1 pops (shift up);
a 3-bit count/valid tracks emptiness. No wrong-path pollution, so no
checkpoint/repair is needed (3-cycle update lag is harmless: callee has to
execute >=2 instrs before its ret).
Predecode of the raw fetched word: is_ret = opcode 1100111 && funct3==0 &&
rd==0 && rs1==1 && instr[31:20]==0 (imm 0, so the target is just rs1 -- no
adder is needed to verify). pred_ret = is_ret && stack non-empty && !stall-gated
like pred_taken; next_pc = pred_ret ? ras_q[0] : (existing JAL/branch/pc+4 mux).
The pred_taken output is also set for pred_ret so EX does not redirect on the
usual `actual_taken ^ pred_taken` term; two new bundle fields, pred_ret and
pred_tgt[31:2] (+31 FF), travel IF->ID/EX.
EX verification stays a tiny cone off op1 flops: ret_ok = (rs1[31:1] ==
pred_tgt[31:1]) && rs1[1:0]==0 -- an equality tree, no carry chain, so it is
shallower than the branch compare that already ends at redir_q. redirect_raw
becomes ((actual_taken ^ pred_taken) || (pred_ret && !ret_ok)) && !redir_q &&
!stall, with the existing !misalign_fault qualification kept for non-ret
cases; for a mispredicted pred_ret the redirect target is
misalign_jump ? pc+4 : jump_target (so a misaligned ret traps and resumes
linearly, as pc_fwd/trap checks in riscv-formal require). redirect_target_d
tests is_jalr/pred_ret before the `pred_taken ? pc+4` arm. JALR without a
prediction (empty stack, imm != 0, other registers) behaves exactly as today.
Squash/ex_busy/divider gating is untouched because the redirect still goes
through redir_q. Risks: +~35 FF and a 31-bit XOR/AND tree on the redirect_raw D
cone (expected shallower than the compare); pc D gains one more mux input
fed from a flop. Must confirm with `make timing` that Fmax does not drop
(the compare->redir_q and imem->predecode->pc legs are in the tied wall).

title: Carry pc+4 and the IF-computed branch/JAL target through ID/EX; delete the EX pc adders
motivation:
After the registered-redirect merge (r6s1, 99.26 MHz) the worst-path wall is a tie of
ID/EX-operand -> carry chain -> result mux -> forward AND-OR families. EX still contains
five 30-32-bit adders that only recompute values IF already has: `in.pc + 4` (JAL/JALR
link into early_result, the pred_taken fall-back redirect target, pc_next),
`in.pc + in.imm` twice (branch_target for the redirect target / misalign check, and the
JAL jump_target). IF forms pc+4 (next_pc) and pc+imm_B/imm_J (pred_target) every cycle from
the same pc and the same raw instruction word that ID/EX captures. r7s0 showed that taking
the jump-link pc+4 leg out of the EX result tail alone is worth ~+2% Fmax (101.2 vs 99.26),
and the pc+imm -> jump_target -> redirect_target_d cone shares the same ID/EX.pc / ID/EX.imm
fanout. Registering the two values (62 flops, they cost no logic in EX) removes ~5 adder
chains (~150 ALU cells) from the timed netlist and the pc/imm fanout from the EX head. All of
it is flop-to-flop with no new logic on any late path, and CPI is unchanged by construction.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add two fields to id_ex_t: `pc4` (= IF's pc + 4, already computed for next_pc) and `tgt`
(= IF's pred_target = pc + (imem_data[3] ? imm_j : imm_b), computed regardless of whether
the prediction was taken or the target is aligned). if_stage exposes both on if_id_t
(new `pc4`, `tgt` fields; no extra adder: the same signals that already feed next_pc),
and id_stage latches them under the existing `!stall` data-flop enable (no reset/flush
needed; they are data fields only consumed for valid branch/JAL/jump ops).
In ex_stage: branch_target = in.tgt (valid for is_branch); jump_target = is_jalr ?
{jalr_sum[31:1],1'b0} : in.tgt (JAL's pc+imm_J == tgt since imm_gen J == imm_j);
the JAL/JALR link is in.pc4; redirect_target_d = in.pred_taken ? in.pc4 : (is_jump ?
jump_target : branch_target); pc_next's pc+4 arms use in.pc4. The misalign checks read
tgt[1:0] / jump_target[1:0] exactly as before (tgt keeps bit 1 from imm[1], so the
misaligned-target trap and suppressed redirect behave identically; JALR still uses
jalr_sum). `jalr_sum = rs1 + imm` (dmem address / JALR target) stays. Net: -5 adders

redirect-target cone from the EX head/tail, lowers ID/EX.pc and ID/EX.imm fanout and
routing congestion, so the placer gets a slightly easier EX; ~+3-5% Fmax. Must be verified

did not move (they are untouched).

title: One shared subtract chain for ADD/SUB/SLT/SLTU/branch compare, and load-use bubbles leave the ID/EX data-flop enable cone
motivation:
After r6s1 (230.30, 99.26 MHz) the top timing paths are a tied wall that all start
at an ID/EX operand flop (op1/op2, fanout ~80) and all run through a 32-bit carry
chain: the ALU add/sub chain, the SLT/SLTU compare chain (ending at alu_result[0]),
and the separate branch-compare chain in ex_stage (ending at redir_q, branch_taken ->
misalign_fault -> ctrl.reg_write). Three independent 32-bit chains hang off the same
two operand flops, and the ID/EX data flops also take an enable (`!stall_id`) that
includes the load-use compare (raw imem rs field -> 5-bit compare -> stall_id ->

title: Registered fetch slice (IF/ID flop + 2-entry skid) with redirect-cycle target fetch: hide dmem/load-use/divide stalls behind fetch
motivation:
Every predictor-only idea on this head is capped by the redirect cost (~70k redirects x 2
bubbles = ~3.3% of 4.31M cycles; the RAS in r7s2 recovered 0.67% and lost on Fmax), so none can
clear the 4.6% acceptance bar. The one IPC pool that is large enough is the backend stall
cycles (dmem stall on 22% of loads/stores, load-use, MUL/JAL late-result consumers, divider):
during each of them stall_if freezes the PC and the word the imem delivered that cycle
(78% of cycles) is thrown away and re-fetched later, so fetch-side slots are lost one-for-one.
r6s2 measured the ceiling: a 2-entry fetch queue took cycles 4240287 -> 3998551 (-5.7%).
It lost on Fmax (81 vs 93 MHz) only because, on the head of that day, it sat in front of decode
(queue-vs-fetch 2:1 word mux feeding decoder / regfile read / load-use compare) and its flush
hung off the combinational EX `redirect` (critical path was EX op2 -> compare -> redirect -> pc D).
On the current head `redirect` is a flop (redir_q) and imem_data in the timed netlist is a flop
(LFSR), so a registered fetch slice is timing-neutral for the ID cone by construction, and the
pc clock-enable stops depending on the load-use compare / dmem_stall / ex_busy cone.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Insert a real fetch slice between IF and ID: an elastic buffer made of one IF/ID output
register FD {pc, instr, pred_taken, valid} plus a 2-entry skid FIFO SK (same payload). Decode,
imm_gen, the regfile read addresses, the fwd_select compares and the hazard-unit load-use compare
all read FD.instr (flops) instead of io_imemData, so there is NO mux between imem_data and the
ID cone (the problem that killed r5s2/r6s2); the only new logic on imem_data is its capture into
FD/SK (1 LUT: FD_next = sk_cnt != 0 ? sk_head : imem word) and the unchanged predecode ->
pred_target adder -> pc D path.

Fetch/accept (flop-only ready, so no stall cone on the pc CE):
  f_valid   = io_imemReady
  accept    = f_valid && (sk_cnt != 2)               // sk_cnt is a 2-bit flop count
  pc <= accept ? (pred_taken ? pred_target : pc+4) : pc   (unchanged predecode/BHT/JAL logic)
  A word goes straight into FD when FD is free and SK is empty, otherwise it is pushed on SK;
  FD <= SK head when FD is free and SK is non-empty (simultaneous push+pop keeps full throughput
  because ready depends on the registered count only).
  FD is free when !FD.valid || !stall_id (stall_id = dmem_stall || load_use || ex_busy, i.e. the
  ID/EX register captured or flushed it this cycle).
ID/EX: unchanged `!stall_id` capture, valid = FD.valid. flush_id = (redirect || !FD.valid ||
load_use_hazard) && !dmem_stall && !ex_busy  (the imem_stall term becomes !FD.valid).
load_use_hazard is qualified with FD.valid and uses FD.instr rs1/rs2.

Redirect (keep the penalty at today's 2 bubbles, not 3): when redir_q = 1 the fetch address is
imem_addr = redir_q ? redir_tgt_q : pc (flop-only mux on the output address; the cosim imem is a
combinational function of the address). The word fetched that cycle replaces the buffer: FD and SK
are flushed (valid <= 0, sk_cnt <= 0) and FD <= {redirect_target, imem word, pred_taken=0} if
io_imemReady, with pc <= redirect_target + 4 (no prediction on that single fetch -- this keeps
redir_q/redir_tgt_q off the BHT index and the pred_target adder; the cost is <=0.3% from a
branch/JAL sitting exactly on a redirect target) or pc <= redirect_target if imem_ready = 0.
The existing EX squash (`ex_busy || redir_q` bubble, `!redir_q` gating of redirect_raw and the
divider start) is untouched, so the wrong-path op A in EX and the word B in FD are killed exactly
as today, and the target T is in EX at t+3 as before. `redirect` only touches FD/SK valid flops,
the sk_cnt flops and the FD/pc capture enables -- all driven by the flop redir_q.

Expected effect: cycles 4.31M -> ~4.06M (-5.7% as measured for the 2-entry queue in r6s2, same
redirect penalty), i.e. ~+6% iter/cycle; Fmax should be neutral to slightly better (the worst path
is EX op2 -> ALU -> alu_result / EX forward at ~15.3 ns and is not touched; the pc CE no longer
carries the load-use compare, dmem_stall and ex_busy; no redirect NOP-mask on the imem word).
Area ~+190 FF (FD 66 + two SK entries 132), ~+150 LUT; well inside the 20k-LUT part.
Verify with `make timing`: the legs to watch are the FD CE (id_hold compare -> 66 flop CE), the
predecode -> pred_target -> pc D path, and the FD/SK D-mux. If the FD CE is critical, accept only
when sk_cnt == 0 for the CE variant and give back some of the hidden stalls.

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-003-r8s2 (regression, +2.79%): Putting the 2-entry fetch buffer behind an IF/ID flop (FD + skid, with decode / regfile read / load-use compare reading FD flops, a flop-only `accept`, and the redirect-cycle fetch from `redir_tgt_q`) turned the fetch-queue family from a loss (r5s2, r6s2 -6.92%) into a net gain (236.72 vs the 230.30 head), but that is only about half of the ~5.7% cycle ceiling and stays under the ~4.6% acceptance bar, so hiding dmem / load-use / divide stalls behind fetch looks capped near +3% net on this head — post-change cycles and `make timing` were not captured, so whether the shortfall is stalls still not hidden or Fmax lost on the FD CE / skid D-mux / predecode -> pc legs is unverified, and a retry must report both before adding more buffering.

title: Pre-decode DSP/load-align controls into flops and delete false late terms (compare->reg_write, DSP decode) from EX/MEM
motivation:
The head (r6s1, 99.26 MHz) and every follow-up since sit on a balanced ~9.8-10.0 ns wall; the
logged worst paths of the last attempts name three different cones that are pure LUT-depth
artifacts rather than real dependencies: (a) r7s0 seed-0 worst = adder/compare chain ->
misalign_fault -> ctrl.reg_write D (36 cells) -- logically false, because a branch never writes
rd (decoder gives reg_write=0 for BRANCH), so only misalign_jump can ever clear reg_write, but
synthesis cannot know that and keeps the late branch_taken term on the reg_write flop; (b) r8s2
worst = ctrl.alu_op flop -> mul_q D (6 cells): alu_op is re-decoded in EX for mul_sa/mul_sb
(the 33rd operand bit a[31]&sa feeding the DSP) and for sel_mul_lo/sel_mul_hi/ex_busy/redir_q
gating on the mul_q flop D/CE, i.e. 2 LUTs before the DSP and a gated mux after it; (c) the
dmem BSRAM read (large clock-to-out) -> shift-by-addr[1:0] -> width/sext case -> forward AND-OR
-> op1/op2 D, where the width/sext/addr decode is recomputed from EX/MEM flops every cycle.
Everything needed to remove these LUTs is known a cycle early (decode in ID, address low bits
from the fast end of the rs1+imm adder), so it can be registered at zero CPI cost and a handful
of flops. Prior single-family fixes (r6s0, r7s0, r8s1 ~ +2%) were not additive because only one
or two of the tied families moved; this change targets the three non-adder families together
and is IPC-neutral (cycles stay 4309869).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Four small, IPC-neutral edits that each remove 1-2 LUT levels from a path in the tied wall:

1. ex_stage: clear ctrl.reg_write only on misalign_jump (not misalign_fault). Branches have
   reg_write=0 already, so the compare-chain -> misalign_branch -> reg_write leg is logically
   redundant. Keep is_illegal = misalign_fault (RVFI-only, pruned from the timed netlist) and keep
   the redirect suppression, but compute the branch misalign term from an ID-predecoded flop
   (bmis = is_branch && instr[8], i.e. imm_b[1]; pc is always word aligned so target[1] = imm[1])
   ANDed with branch_taken, instead of the adder-derived branch_target[1:0] != 0 compare. Fold it
   into actual_taken so redirect_raw = ((branch_taken & ~bmis) | is_jump) ^ pred_taken, gated by
   ~misalign_jump & ~redir_q & ~stall (a bmis branch is never predicted taken, so this equals the
   old expression).

2. DSP controls pre-decoded in ID: add id_ex ctrl bits mul_sa, mul_sb (MULH/MULHSU, MULH),
   sel_mul_lo, sel_mul_hi, computed in id_stage from the raw word and registered under the same
   reset/flush/!stall rule as the other ctrl bits (flush clears them). alu.sv takes mul_sa/mul_sb
   as input ports (keep the op-based computation when the test_alu.py harness instantiates it
   without them: tie to the op decode inside a default wrapper or add input ports with a
   generate/parameter so test_alu.py still checks bit-exact results). The ALTOPS branch stays
   consistent. ex_stage uses the sel_* flops directly: mul_result = ({32{sel_lo}} & lo) |
   ({32{sel_hi}} & hi), so DSP -> mul_q is one LUT plus the CE.

3. mul_q update simplified to `if (reset) mul_q <= 0; else if (!stall) mul_q <= mul_result;`
   (drop the ex_busy||redir_q zeroing). It is safe: sel_* are 0 for a divide, so mul_result is 0
   while ex_busy; a wrong-path MUL squashed by redir_q lands a product in mul_q next to a bubble
   in reg_q (ctrl=0, valid=0), and every consumer of EX/MEM.alu_result|mul_q (the MEM-now forward
   term via mem_we, MEM/WB alu_result via reg_write&&valid, RVFI rd_wdata via rd_wen) is gated by
   reg_write which is 0 for the bubble. This removes ex_busy (alu_op decode + valid + div_done)
   and redir_q from the mul_q D cone.

4. Load-align one-hot selects registered in EX/MEM: from jalr_sum[1:0] (fast low adder bits)
   and ctrl.mem_width/mem_sext (flops) compute in ex_stage lane_b0..lane_b3, ld_word,
   ld_half_hi, ld_sext_en and carry them in ex_mem_t; mem_stage load_data becomes a flat
   one-hot AND-OR of dmem_rdata bytes (byte k = lane_k & rdata[8k+:8]) with the sign bit taken
   as an AND-OR of rdata[7/15/23/31] with the same one-hot lane flags, instead of shift-by-
   addr[1:0]*8 followed by a width/sext case. Misaligned accesses are already gated by
   mem_misalign and may produce arbitrary load_data (reg_write is cleared). Keep the existing
   mem_addr/byte_mask/RVFI logic unchanged.

Expected: DSP, compare->flag and load-align legs all lose >= 1 LUT (~0.6-0.9 ns each), so the
tied wall moves down together; +16..+20 FF, ~0 LUT. IPC is unchanged by construction.

title: Registered fetch slice (FD flop + 2-entry skid, flop-only accept) with the DSP product leg predecoded off the Fmax wall
motivation:
IPC and Fmax are both pinned on this head. Cycles are 4.31M for 10 iterations; the imem 22% stall floor
is ~3.9M, and the remaining ~10% is backend stall cycles (dmem stall on 22% of loads/stores, load-use,
MUL/JAL late-result consumers, divider) during which stall_if freezes the PC and throws away the word
the imem delivered that cycle. A decoupled fetch is the only structural lever left with a >5% ceiling:
r6s2 measured -5.7% cycles and r8s2 (FD register + 2-entry skid, decode/regfile/fwd compare reading FD
flops, flop-only accept, redirect-cycle fetch from redir_tgt_q) measured cycles 4086552 vs 4309869
(-5.2%, i.e. +5.5% iter/cycle, formal and cosim both passed). So the IPC half is already proven and
essentially at its ceiling; r8s2 only missed the 4.6% acceptance bar (236.72 vs 240.9 needed) because the
median Fmax over the 3 placement seeds fell to 96.735 (seeds 100.23 / 96.74 / 96.74) against 99.258
(100.29 / 99.26 / 99.26) on the head. Its reported worst path was the DSP leg

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Part A -- fetch slice, as in r8s2 (this is the structural change that carries the IPC gain):
Insert a real elastic buffer between IF and ID: one IF/ID output register FD {pc, instr, pred_taken,
valid} plus a 2-entry skid FIFO SK of the same payload with a 2-bit flop count sk_cnt. Decode, imm_gen,
regfile read addresses, fwd_select compares and the hazard-unit load-use compare all read FD.instr
(flops), so there is no mux between imem_data and the ID cone (the problem that sank r5s2/r6s2); the
only new logic on imem_data is its capture into FD/SK (FD_next = sk_cnt != 0 ? sk_head : imem word).
  f_valid = io_imemReady;  accept = f_valid && (sk_cnt != 2)     // flop-only: no stall cone on the pc CE
  pc <= accept ? (pred_taken ? pred_target : pc+4) : pc           // predecode/BHT/pred_target unchanged
  FD free = !FD.valid || !stall_id (stall_id = dmem_stall || load_use || ex_busy)
  a word goes to FD when FD is free and SK empty, else is pushed on SK; FD <= SK head when FD free and SK
  non-empty. ID/EX capture is unchanged (!stall_id), valid = FD.valid.
  flush_id = (redirect || !FD.valid || load_use_hazard) && !dmem_stall && !ex_busy;
  load_use_hazard is qualified with FD.valid and reads FD.instr rs1/rs2.
Redirect keeps today's 2 bubbles: while redir_q = 1 the fetch address is imem_addr = redir_q ? redir_tgt_q : pc
(a flop-only mux on the output address), FD and SK are flushed (valid <= 0, sk_cnt <= 0) and FD is loaded
with {redirect_target, imem word, pred_taken = 0} if io_imemReady, with pc <= redirect_target + 4 (or
pc <= redirect_target when not ready). The existing EX squash (`ex_busy || redir_q` bubble, !redir_q gating
of redirect_raw and the divider start) is untouched. `redirect` only reaches FD/SK valid flops, sk_cnt
and the FD/pc capture enables, all driven by the flop redir_q; nothing from the late EX compare is
added to any D cone.

op-based decode as the default so test_alu.py still checks the same results (e.g. by adding
optional mul_sa/mul_sb override ports used by ex_stage, or by choosing the ALU_MUL* encodings so the sign

(~0.5-0.8 ns) on the DSP family, so the median seed no longer lands on it.

`make timing` must show the DSP leg off the top of the report; if the FD CE (FD-free compare -> 66 flop CE)
or the FD/SK D-mux is critical, restrict accept to sk_cnt == 0 for the CE term.

title: Decoupled predicted-fetch queue: IF/ID flop head + 4-entry flop FIFO (flop-only accept) to hide imem stalls behind backend stalls
motivation:
Prediction quality is exhausted on this head: total redirect cost is ~70k x 2
bubbles = ~3.2% of the ~4.3M timed cycles (r7s2's RAS recovered only 0.64% and
lost on Fmax), so no direction/target predictor can clear the 4.6% acceptance
bar by IPC alone. What the predictor *front end* can still buy is fetch
decoupling: the predicted fetch stream (BHT + JAL always-taken, already
zero-bubble) runs ahead of decode, so the 22% imem-not-ready cycles are
absorbed by words that were fetched during backend stall cycles instead of
becoming bubbles. Backend stall pool today (cycles in which stall_if freezes
the PC and the word that imem DID deliver, 78% of the time, is thrown away
and re-fetched): dmem stall on ~22% of ~830k loads/stores (~180k), load-use /
JAL / MUL late-result consumer stalls (~150-200k), divider, redirect bubbles.
With imem delivering 0.78 words/cycle and ~2.9M instructions the hard bound
is ~3.75M cycles vs 4.31M today (~13%). Measured points: r6s2's depth-2 queue
cut cycles 4240287 -> 3998551 (-5.7%, 2 entries, redirect-gated) and r8s2's
registered FD + 2-entry skid netted +2.79% (236.72 vs 230.30) with Fmax
roughly neutral -- i.e. depth 2 captures only about half of the bound, the
rest needs more buffered words because a dmem/load-use stall run of 2-4 cycles
fills a 2-entry skid before the next imem stall arrives. Depth is cheap here
(a few hundred FF/LUT of a 20k-LUT part) as long as no logic is added on
imem_data -> decode / regfile read / forward compare cones.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the combinational IF/ID bundle with a registered fetch queue whose
head is the ID-facing flop set and whose tail is a small flop FIFO; keep the
existing BHT/JAL predecode + pred_target adder + pc D path exactly as is
(imem_data -> predecode -> pc D unchanged), and take everything *downstream*
of imem_data off the stall cone.

Structure (all in if_stage.sv; if_id_t payload {pc, instr, valid, pred_taken}
per entry):
  - Q[0] = FD is the head: id_stage / decoder / imm_gen / regfile read
    addresses / fwd_select compares / hazard load-use compare all read FD.instr
    (flops), so no mux sits between a stall-dependent source and the ID cone.
  - Q[1..3] is a 3-entry shifting FIFO (head-always-at-Q[0], valid bits +
    a 2-bit flop count `cnt` of occupied entries behind FD). Each entry's D is a
    3:1 mux {hold, shift-from-next, imem word} selected by flops plus the
    pop signal (pop = FD consumed = !stall_id || !FD.valid).
  - accept = io_imemReady && (cnt != 3)  -- flop count + ready only, so the pc
    CE is NOT a function of load_use_hazard / dmem_stall / ex_busy any more
    (today stall_if = load_use || imem_stall || dmem_stall || ex_busy sits on
    the pc enable together with the pred_target adder). pc <= accept ?
    (pred_taken ? pred_target : pc+4) : pc.
  - The word fetched this cycle goes to FD if FD is empty/consumed and cnt==0,
    else is pushed at slot (cnt - pop). pred_taken rides with the word; the BHT
    is still trained from EX/MEM exactly as today.
  - Redirect (redir_q is a flop): all Q valid bits and cnt clear; to keep
    today's 2-bubble recovery (an extra FD stage would otherwise make it 3) the
    fetch address in the redirect cycle is io_imemAddr = redir_q ? redir_tgt_q
    : pc (flop-only 2:1 mux on an output that feeds only the imem port) and the
    word fetched then is written straight into FD with pc/pred_taken from
    redir_tgt_q / 0 (no prediction for that single fetch, so redir_tgt_q stays
    off the BHT index and the pred_target adder), with pc <= redir_tgt_q + 4
    if imem_ready else pc <= redir_tgt_q. The existing EX squash
    (`ex_busy || redir_q` bubble in EX/MEM and mul_q, redirect_raw gated by
    !redir_q, divider start gated by !redir_q) is untouched.
  - ID/EX capture is unchanged (`!stall_id`), valid = FD.valid;
    flush_id = (redirect || !FD.valid || load_use_hazard) && !dmem_stall &&
    !ex_busy (the imem_stall term becomes !FD.valid); load_use_hazard is
    qualified with FD.valid and uses FD.instr rs1/rs2. hazard_unit's stall_if
    output is dropped from the pc CE (kept only as the pop gating).
Stale-prediction note: words are predicted up to 3 words ahead of the BHT
training (EX/MEM); the extra mispredicts are expected to be small (<0.2%) and
are flushed by the same registered redirect.

Expected: cycles 4.31M -> ~3.95M (depth 4 recovers most of the ~13% bound that
depth 2 only half captured), i.e. ~+8-9% iter/cycle; Fmax assumed within ~-3%
(the timed legs unchanged: ALU/EX forward and BSRAM load-align -> op D; the
pc CE gets *lighter*, FD/queue D-mux is 2 LUT levels from the imem word, the
imem_data -> predecode -> pc D adder path is unchanged). Net ~+5-6%.
Verification obligations for the implementer: (1) cosim cycle count must be
reported and compared to 4240287; (2) `make timing` worst paths must be
checked on the FD/queue CE (pop = !stall_id -> ~100 flop CEs: if it is
critical, pop only from FD.valid && !dmem_stall && !ex_busy && !load_use via a
registered/pre-decoded copy, or accept only when cnt==0 for the CE variant),
the queue D-mux, and imem_data -> predecode -> pc D; (3) riscv-formal liveness
/ pc_fwd / unique must pass -- rvfi order and pc_next are produced downstream of
EX/MEM and are unchanged, wrong-path words are never marked valid after a
redirect because Q is cleared by the flop redir_q.
If depth 4 shows Fmax loss from fan-out on pop/CE, fall back to depth 3
(cnt != 2) rather than abandoning the queue; do not add the RAS or a larger BHT
in this change.

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-003-r9s2 (improvement, +13.83%): A depth-4 fetch queue (FD flop head feeding decode/regfile-read/load-use compare, 3-entry shifting flop FIFO, `accept = imem_ready && cnt != 3` so the pc CE no longer contains load_use/dmem_stall/ex_busy, redirect-cycle fetch from `redir_tgt_q`) took fitness 230.30 -> 262.14, about 2x the predicted +6% net and close to the ~13% cycle bound, where the same FD+skid structure at depth 2 (r8s2) netted only +2.79% — so the earlier "fetch buffering is capped near +3%" conclusion was a depth limit, not a structural one (dmem/load-use/divide stall runs of 2-4 cycles overflow a 2-entry skid before the next imem stall), and with every queue read/CE on flops and the pc CE made lighter, going from 2 to 4 entries cost little Fmax; when a buffer is flop-only on its consumer and producer cones, size it to the stall-run length (post-change cycles and `make timing` were not captured, so the split between cycles saved and Fmax kept is inferred).

title: Fuse load-align into ID forward AND-OR with registered lane/sign selects + DSP/reg_write predecode
motivation:
After the r9s2 fetch queue merged, the worst path is no longer imem -> fwd compare (that cone now starts at the FD flops)
but dmem BSRAM DO -> mem_stage load-align/sign-extend -> id_stage forward AND-OR -> ID/EX.op1/op2 D
(log: from dmem_3_..._s to cpu/u_id/reg_q.op1_30, 16.127 ns, 9 cells, modules u_mem > u_id). The BSRAM output is the
latest-arriving signal in the design, yet today it passes through a generic 4:1 byte shift, a width/sext case on
decoded ctrl bits (extra LUT level), and only then the s?_mld AND and the OR with the other forward sources: ~4 LUT
levels behind the BSRAM. Every select that gates those terms (rs compare vs MEM rd, mem_is_load, width, sext,
addr[1:0]) is a flop-derived value known several ns before the BSRAM data, so it can be reduced to a small set of
one-hot select signals ahead of time and the late BSRAM bits should see exactly one AND-OR (2 LUT levels), merged
into the operand D input. Prior r9s0 showed that registered one-hot predecode of load-align / DSP / reg_write
controls is an IPC-neutral Fmax lever (+8% at unchanged cycles, 230 -> 249) but it merged behind r9s2 and never
fused the s?_mld gate into the data AND-OR.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Pure Fmax change, cycle count unchanged (target 4065578 cycles). Three pieces that cut a LUT level from the tied
cones (BSRAM -> operand D, DSP -> mul_q, branch compare -> ctrl.reg_write):

1. Registered load lane/sign selects. In ex_stage compute from in.ctrl.mem_width, in.ctrl.mem_sext and
   jalr_sum[1:0] (2-bit low add, early) a set of one-hot select flops carried in EX/MEM (new ex_mem_t fields,
   zeroed on bubble, held on stall like the rest of reg_q). With W/H0/H1/B0..B3 the word/half-at-addr[1]/byte-lane
   decodes:
     group A (result bits 7:0):   dA0=W|H0|B0 (r[i]), dA1=B1 (r[i+8]), dA2=H1|B2 (r[i+16]), dA3=B3 (r[i+24])
     group B (bits 15:8):         dB0=W|H0 (r[i]), dB2=H1 (r[i+16]); sign selects gB7=sext&B0, gB15=sext&B1,
                                  gB23=sext&B2, gB31=sext&B3 (byte only; half/word bits 15:8 are data)
     group C (bits 31:16):        dC=W (r[i]); sign selects gC7=sext&B0, gC15=sext&(B1|H0), gC23=sext&B2,
                                  gC31=sext&(B3|H1)
   Misaligned accesses need no special case: the trap already clears reg_write via mem_we_nxt, so neither the
   forward (s?_mld needs mem_we) nor the regfile write ever consumes a misaligned lane value.
2. Fuse the load term into the id_stage operand AND-OR. Export raw dmem_rdata (io_dmemRData) into id_stage and
   build op1_d/op2_d as one flat AND-OR: the load contribution for result bit i is
     (rdata[i] & {s_mld & use_ok & dX}) | (rdata[i+8] & ...) | ... | (rdata[7|15|23|31] & {s_mld & use_ok & g*})
   where s?_mld, !use_pc (op1) / !use_imm (op2) and the lane/sign select flop are ANDed EARLY (flop -> 2-LUT
   compare -> AND, ready ~4 ns, long before the BSRAM data), and every non-load source (EX-now, MEM-alu, WB, regfile,
   pc, imm) is pre-ORed into one `rest` term. The BSRAM bits then see only 2 LUT levels (<=5 data terms + `rest`)
   before the ID/EX D pin instead of ~4. Keep mem_stage.load_data (built from the same registered selects, so the
   two views cannot disagree) for MEM/WB.read_data and for the RVFI-only rv1_d/rv2_d, which synthesis prunes from
   the timed netlist.
3. r9s0's proven predecode, re-applied on the new head: (a) decode mul_sa/mul_sb/sel_mul_lo/sel_mul_hi in ID into

title: Register the raw 64-bit DSP product at EX/MEM and select lo/hi after the flop (DSP leg becomes DSP -> flop)
motivation:
After the r9s2 fetch queue the CoreMark cycle count (4.066M) sits within a few percent of the imem
22%-stall fetch floor, and depth 2 -> 4 only moved cycles by 0.5%, so IPC is saturated and the only
remaining lever is Fmax. The head's placement seeds are 92.3 / 106.6 / 106.6 MHz: seed 0 is the
9-cell BSRAM -> load-align -> forward -> op1 D path, but the median (what is scored) is set by a
6-cell path at 9.38 ns, and the 6-cell family on this core has been the DSP leg every time it was
reported (ID/EX.alu_op -> mul_sa/mul_sb -> 33x33 DSP -> sel_mul_lo/hi AND-OR -> mul_q, r8s2/r7s1).
Today the lo/hi half select (and its zeroing for non-MUL ops) sits between the DSP output and the
mul_q flops, so the DSP's combinational delay is followed by a LUT and a CE/clear mux before the D pin.
Caveat: the attribution of the median-seed path to the DSP leg is inferred from the 6-cell path length
and from earlier reports (a `make timing` run on the current head was not completed in this session);
the implementer should confirm the worst path with `make timing` before and after the change.

title: Predicted-fetch L0 instruction store: 128-word direct-mapped LUT-RAM cache read by the fetch pc so hits bypass imem backpressure
motivation:
Direction/target prediction is exhausted on this head: all redirects together
(~70k x 2 bubbles) are ~3.2% of the ~4.07M timed cycles, and r7s2's RAS (0.64%
IPC ceiling) already lost on Fmax. No bimodal->gshare / BTB / RAS change can clear
the 4.6% acceptance bar by IPC alone, so this slot goes to the other thing the
predicted fetch stream (the BHT/JAL stream and fetch queue of r9s2) is limited by:
instruction supply. It is an instruction-store change attached to the fetch
stream, not a direction predictor.

The machine is now fetch-bound. imem_ready is low ~22% of cycles, so fetch
delivers at most 0.78 words/cycle. Timed region = 2.92M retired instructions
(measured with the reference ISS on bench/programs/coremark.elf, markers
0x10000100/0x10000104) + ~140k wrong-path fetch slots ~= 3.1M words / 0.78
~= 3.97M cycles, vs 4.07M observed -- the r9s2 queue already hides the backend
stalls, so the bus is the bottleneck. The backend-only bound (instructions +
dmem stalls ~180k + load-use/JAL/MUL consumer stalls ~150-200k + redirect
bubbles ~140k) is ~3.45-3.55M cycles, ~13% below today. It cannot be reached
while every fetched word has to cross the 22%-stalled bus.

CoreMark re-executes small kernels (crc, matrix, state machine, list
find/sort). I measured direct-mapped hit rates on the real timed PC trace
(2,922,017 fetches, word-granular, no prefetch, cold start included):
    64 words 71.5% | 128 words 83.3% | 256 words 93.8% | 512 words 97.0% | 1024 words 98.9%
A 128-word (512 B) store already lifts the effective fetch rate from 0.78 to
1/(0.833 + 0.167/0.78) = ~0.955 words/cycle, above the backend-bound rate of the
rest of the machine.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a small direct-mapped L0 instruction store inside if_stage.sv, looked up
with the fetch address every cycle, so that a hit is accepted into the fetch
queue without waiting for io_imemReady. The cache only changes WHEN a word is
accepted, never WHICH word is fetched: the pc / instruction stream, RVFI, the
decoder, hazard unit and backend are untouched.

Structure (all in if_stage.sv, a localparam sets the depth, default 128):
  - fa = imem_addr = redirect ? redirect_target : pc (two flops and a 2:1 LUT:
    the existing imem port mux). idx = fa[8:2], tag = fa[19:9] (11 bits; all
    legal fetch addresses are < 0x100000).
  - Data array 128x32 and tag array 128x11 are asynchronous-read LUT-RAM
    (SSRAM) with a synchronous write port: `(* syn_ramstyle =
    "distributed_ram" *)` on a `logic [W-1:0] mem [0:127]` written in an
    always_ff. ~270 LUT-RAM LUTs + read muxes; the 128-entry valid vector is
    plain flops (reset to 0), which keeps the arrays reset-free.
  - hit = valid[idx] && tag_rd == fa[19:9].
    word = hit ? cache_data : imem_data  (one LUT level in front of the
    existing predecode; predecode, pred_target adder, w = {pc, word,
    pred_taken}, q0..q3 and the redirect-cycle write into q0 are unchanged).
  - Handshake: have = imem_ready || hit; accept = have && !qv[3]; in the
    redirect cycle qv <= {3'b0, have} and pc <= have ? redirect_target + 4 :
    redirect_target. have/accept derive from flops + LUT-RAM only (no
    load-use / dmem-stall / divider term), so the r9s2 rule "keep stall terms
    off the pc CE" holds.
  - Fill: whenever imem delivers a word that missed (fill = imem_ready &&
    !hit, independent of qv[3], including the redirect-cycle fetch):
    data[idx] <= imem_data, tag[idx] <= tag, valid[idx] <= 1. Written only on
    misses, so one write port suffices. Filling when the queue is full is a
    free prefetch of the word that would have been dropped and re-fetched.
  - Coherence: snoop stores. snoop = (io_dmemWEn != 0) && io_dmemReady (the
    cycle the store actually completes, not the stalled cycles: otherwise a
    refill between the snoop and the write would resurrect the stale word).
    A second async read port on the tag array at io_dmemAddr[8:2]; when
    valid && tag matches, valid[idx] <= 0. A snoop to the same idx as a
    same-cycle fill wins (valid cleared). This makes the L0 coherent with all
    stores at MEM, which is stricter than the ISA needs (FENCE.I stays a NOP,
    selftest/cosim programs that store to code still match the ISS).
  - Formal: riscv-formal drives imem_data as a free input every cycle; a hit
    then returns an earlier random word, but the core still reports the
    instruction it actually executed as rvfi_insn, and the insn/pc_fwd/unique
    /liveness checks are properties of that reported stream, so they stay
    valid. test_pipeline.py instantiating the core needs no change (no core
    port changes); if it instantiates if_stage directly, tie the new
    snoop_en / snoop_addr inputs to 0.

Expected effect: ~12% fewer cycles (4.07M -> ~3.6M: the machine goes from
fetch-bound to backend-bound), area +~1000 LUT (3892 -> ~4900, well under the
10000 target), FF +~140 (valid vector; arrays are LUT-RAM).

Timing plan (the part to verify in `make timing`): the hit signal is
pc flop -> redirect mux -> LUT-RAM async read -> 11-bit compare -> &valid,
roughly 5-6 ns after the clock edge, so it lands about when imem_data (an LFSR
flop in the timed netlist) is available plus 4-5 ns. Downstream of it:
(a) accept -> ins[] -> q1..q3 D-mux (~200 flops): ~10 ns total, inside the
~16 ns wall; (b) hit -> word mux -> predecode -> pred_off select -> 30-bit
pred_target adder -> pc D mux: ~12-13 ns. If (b) becomes the worst path,
take the late `hit` off the adder: compute pred_off/is_jal/is_br from the
cache word and from imem_data separately (each only needs its own word) and
let hit drive one final 2:1 select before the pc D mux, or store predecoded
{is_jal, is_br, pred_off[20:1]} bits in the data array so the hit leg needs
no predecode. If LUT-RAM inference fails or Fmax drops >4%, fall back to a
64-entry flop array (syn_ramstyle = "registers", 71.5% hit rate) or try 256
entries (93.8%) if timing has slack; the depth is a single localparam.

New inputs snoop_en and snoop_addr[19:2].
Wire the store snoop into u_if: snoop_en = (io_dmemWEn != 4'b0) && io_dmemReady, snoop_addr = io_dmemAddr. No change to the core port list or RVFI.

Add the 128-word direct-mapped LUT-RAM L0 (data + tag arrays with async read from fa = redirect ? redirect_target : pc, valid flop vector, fill-on-miss write port gated by imem_ready && !hit, second async tag read port + valid clear for the store snoop); select word = hit ? cache_data : imem_data in front of the existing predecode; have = imem_ready || hit; accept = have && !qv[3]; redirect-cycle qv/pc next-state use have. New inputs snoop_en and snoop_addr[19:2].
Wire the store snoop into u_if: snoop_en = (io_dmemWEn != 4'b0) && io_dmemReady, snoop_addr = io_dmemAddr. No change to the core port list or RVFI.

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-003-r10s2 (regression, -43.84%): A 128-word direct-mapped L0 instruction store (async LUT-RAM data/tag read at `fa = redirect ? redirect_target : pc`, 11-bit tag compare, 128-flop `l0_valid` mux, `hit` feeding `have`/`accept`, the word mux ahead of predecode -> 30-bit `pred_target` adder -> pc D, and the ~200-flop queue write enables, plus a second tag array and dmem-store snoop) scored 147.23 vs the 262.14 r9s2 head, and since it cannot add cycles and could save at most ~12%, Fmax fell by roughly half — in the timed netlist `imem_ready`/`imem_data` are already flop-launched, so the cache removes no real delay and only puts a pc -> LUT-RAM -> compare -> `hit` cone (not a flop) onto the accept/pc-CE/queue-D and predecode -> pc legs that r9s2 had just made flop-only; the proposer's 12-13 ns estimate for that cone was never checked with `make timing` (not captured, and whether LUT-RAM inference held is unverified) — don't put any address-indexed lookup or tag compare on the fetch address ahead of `accept`/predecode, since the ~12% cycle ceiling cannot pay for it, and treat fetch-supply changes as closed unless a measured path report shows slack.

title: Register file on dual replicated LUT-RAM (async read) instead of 992 reset/CE flops + two 32:1 flop muxes
motivation:
The head's IPC is within ~3% of the imem-bandwidth ceiling (1 word/cycle at ~78% ready:
4.07M cycles vs ~3.9M fetch-bound), so every remaining gain has to come from Fmax, and the
last five LUT-depth reshuffles (DSP controls, load-align fuse, DSP raw-product register,
unified compare chain, adder removal) were all flat or negative because the worst paths are
a placement/routing-limited wall (~9 cells, 14.5-16 ns in option 0, ~9.4 ns median), not a
single deep leg. What none of them touched is the one structure that is ~half of the whole
netlist: reg_file.sv is 31x32 = 992 flops, each with a sync reset and a 5-bit-decoded write
CE (31 decoders, wb_w_data fanning out to 31 flops per bit), plus two 31:1 x 32-bit read
muxes (~4 LUT/mux levels, ~600+ LUTs) fed by the FD rs1/rs2 address flops. That is ~50% of
the 2027 FFs and a large share of the 3892 LUTs, with high-fanout nets (write data x31,
read address bits x32 bit-slices) landing in the middle of the ID forward cone and
stretching placement of everything around it. Gowin LUT-RAM (RAM16SDP4: sync write, async
read, ~one LUT delay) holds 16x4 bits per cell, so the same two-read-port 32x32 array is
~32 RAM cells + a 2:1 bit-4 mux per port instead of ~1600 cells, and removes both the
reset/CE fanout and the deep read mux.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Rewrite reg_file.sv so each read port has its own 32x32 array declared as inferred
distributed RAM (one write port shared by both copies: write w_data to copy A and copy B at
w_addr under w_en; async reads at rs1_addr / rs2_addr; attribute

fwd_select sel_ram with nz (a != 0) so the AND-OR contributes 0 for x0 (nz is a compare of
FD flops, already computed in fwd_select, so no extra data-path depth). Drop the regfile
reset (RAM has none; Verilator x-initial is 0 and riscv-formal's reg/pc checks use the
DUT-reported rs?_rdata and a symbolic initial register state, so the proof contract is
unchanged). Net effect: ~-900 LUT, ~-1000 FF, the write-data fanout drops from 31 flops/bit
to 2 RAM DI pins/bit per half, the read path FD-flop -> 32:1 flop mux (4 levels) becomes
FD-flop -> LUT-RAM -> bit-4 MUX2 (~2 levels) ahead of the same forward AND-OR, and the freed
area/routing lets the placer pull the ID/EX operand flops, the forward cone and the ALU
closer together. Cycle count is unchanged (read stays combinational in ID, write at WB),
so the fitness change equals the Fmax change; the 4.6% acceptance bar needs the median
Fmax to go from 106.6 to >= ~111.5 MHz. Done only if `make timing` and the Gowin report show
lutram > 0, bsram unchanged (4), and the regfile read leg is not the new worst path; if
inference falls back to BSRAM or to registers the hypothesis is void and should be reported
as such rather than patched around.

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-001-r11s0 (regression, -5.35%): Replacing the 992-flop reset/CE regfile and its two 32:1 flop read muxes with two replicated 32x32 `syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram"` LUT-RAM arrays (async read, no reset, x0 handled by gating `fwd_select.sel_ram` with `nz`) scored 248.11 vs the 262.14 r9s2 head at unchanged cycles, so Fmax fell ~5% instead of gaining the predicted +5% — the premise that deleting ~half the netlist would let the placer pull the ID forward cone together did not hold, since the flop-launched 32:1 read was not what bounded the wall and an async LUT-RAM read (RAM cells at fixed slice sites plus a bit-4 2:1 mux, into the same forward AND-OR -> ID/EX operand D) evidently adds routing/delay on that cone rather than removing it (no post-change `make timing` or Gowin lutram/bsram counts were captured, so whether inference held is unverified) — don't use regfile-to-LUT-RAM or pure area/FF reduction as an Fmax lever unless a measured path report puts the regfile read leg on the worst path.

title: Spend fetch-bound backend slack: raw dmem data into MEM/WB, load align in WB, two-cycle load-use
motivation:
After the r9s2 fetch queue the core is fetch-bound: 2.92M retired instructions at
0.78 words/cycle (22% imem stall) is a ~3.74M-cycle floor against 4.07M observed, while the
backend-only bound (dmem stalls, load-use, redirects) is ~3.5M. Depth 2 -> 4 moved cycles
only 0.5%, so a few extra backend stall cycles are largely absorbed by the 4-entry queue,
whereas Fmax (106.6 MHz) is the only remaining lever and the wall is a set of tied ~9.4 ns
legs. The dmem read data (BSRAM/LUT-RAM output, the latest-arriving signal in the design)
still runs through mem_stage's 4:1 byte shift + width/sext case, then id_stage's forward
AND-OR into ID/EX op1/op2 (9-cell path, u_mem > u_id). r10s0 only trimmed one LUT level off
that leg and landed flat; this removes the leg entirely by trading load-use latency,
which is the cheapest thing to trade now that fetch, not the backend, sets the cycle count.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make the load result a registered value. mem_stage stops computing load_data in the MEM
cycle: MEM/WB captures the raw dmem_rdata word plus predecoded lane/width/sext selects
(from EX/MEM mem_addr[1:0], mem_width, mem_sext; all flop-derived), so the BSRAM output
goes straight to a flop D pin with no logic. wb_stage performs the byte shift and
sign/zero extension from the MEM/WB flops, giving a flop-launched w_data for the regfile
write port and the WB-now forward term (a short flop -> align -> AND-OR path instead of a
BSRAM -> align -> AND-OR path). ID's forward select loses the MEM-load term: a load in MEM
is no longer forwardable, so hazard_unit treats loads as producers whose consumer must be
>= 2 instructions behind: it stalls the consumer in ID while the load sits in EX (as now)
AND while it sits in MEM (new, `mem_is_load && rd match`), after which the value comes from
WB-now. Costs one extra bubble for distance-1 load-use, one for distance-2; the load-use
count in CoreMark's timed region is modest (<=~100k stalls) and the 4-entry fetch queue
hides most of them because the fetch bus is the bottleneck. Non-load producers and
JAL/JALR/MUL* handling are unchanged. dmem_stall/hold_mem_wb behaviour is unchanged
(MEM/WB still keeps its data fields on hold and clears only valid). RVFI mem_rdata /
rd_wdata stay correct because the aligned value is formed in WB from the same raw word.
The fwd_select sel_mem_ld term and the mem_ld_val port are deleted, removing one AND-OR
leg (32 x 2 AND terms) from both operand cones.

Break-even and risk: the extra load-use stalls are estimated at ~+150-250k backend
cycles, of which the queue should hide most because fetch (~3.97M-cycle bound) is slower
than the backend (~3.5M); the realistic cycle cost is ~1-3%. The change therefore needs
>= ~7% Fmax to clear the 4.6% bar. That only holds if the BSRAM -> align -> forward -> op D
leg is on the median placement seed's wall (r10s0 trimmed one LUT off it and was flat, so
this is the unverified part). The implementer should compare cycle count against 4065578
and read `make timing` before and after; if cycles rise > 3% the distance-2 stall should be
dropped for consumers that are not on the rs1 path of a branch/store address.

Drop mem_ld_val term from rest1/rest2 AND-OR and the mem_ld_val port.

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-002-r11s1 (regression, -9.83%): Registering the raw `dmem_rdata` word plus predecoded lane/width/sext selects in MEM/WB, doing the byte shift and sign/zero extension in `wb_stage`, and deleting the `sel_mem_ld` forward term (so `hazard_unit` also stalls a consumer while the load sits in MEM, making load-use 2 cycles) scored 236.37 vs the 262.14 r9s2 head, though the proposal budgeted only ~1-3% cycles and needed ~7% Fmax — so either the 4-entry fetch queue did not hide the extra load-use bubbles (a fetch-bound core still consumes the queue's catch-up slack, only ~0.22 word/cycle, and load-use bubbles cluster on the dependent chains of CoreMark's list/matrix loops) or the new WB-now leg (flop -> align -> forward AND-OR -> op D, plus the added `ex_mem_rd` compare in the `stall_id` cone) cost Fmax, and no post-change cycle count or `make timing` was captured to say which (the proposer's own `make timing` never finished) — the "fetch-bound, so backend latency is free" argument from r9s2's flat 2->4-entry depth result does not license adding load-use latency, so don't trade pipeline latency for Fmax on this head unless the cycle cost is measured first and a path report shows the BSRAM -> align -> operand D leg alone sets the median wall.

title: 128-entry gshare BHT with resolve-time global history, flop-only read, training on the EX/MEM port
motivation:
The head (r9s2 fetch queue, 4.07M cycles) is close to the imem supply bound (~78% words/cycle),
so the only IPC left in the front end is the ~70k redirects, each wasting ~3 fetch slots
(2 bubbles plus wrong-path words). The predictor is a 32-entry bimodal table indexed by pc[6:2]:
CoreMark's hot code (list, matrix, state machine, crc) has far more than 32 static branches, so
entries alias, and a local 2-bit counter cannot capture the correlated branches in
core_state_transition / crcu8. Lessons (r7s2, r10s2) say any front-end change must be
Fmax-neutral by construction: nothing new on imem_data -> predecode -> pc, nothing on
redirect_raw, no address-indexed lookup on the fetch address beyond a flop-fed mux.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
In if_stage.sv replace the 32x2 bimodal array with a 128 x 2-bit table indexed by
pc[8:2] ^ ghr[6:0]. ghr is a 7-bit global history register shifted in the existing BHT
training always_ff (train_en / train_taken, i.e. resolve order, fed from the EX/MEM register),
so there is no speculative-history repair path and no new signal from EX; the history seen by
fetch is ~3-4 branches stale, which costs some accuracy but keeps the read a pure
flop -> 128:1 mux. The training read-modify-write indexes with the EX/MEM pc[8:2] XOR the
history captured with that branch (carry a 7-bit ghr snapshot in a small side register chain,
or reuse the current ghr at train time as an approximation; the simpler approximation is
acceptable). Reset: all counters weakly taken (2'b10), ghr = 0. JAL stays always-taken, JALR
unpredicted, queue/redirect/EX/ID untouched. Expected effect: mispredict rate down ~20-30%
(about 14-20k fewer redirects at ~3 cycles) = ~1-1.5% cycles, about +256 FF, a few hundred LUTs for
the wider read mux. This is a low-probability, Fmax-neutral-by-construction predictor upgrade; the
main risk is that the wider read mux lands on the tied pc-D / pred_taken cone and costs Fmax.

Widen train_idx to ex_mem_w.pc[8:2] (index is XORed with ghr inside if_stage); other signals unchanged.

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-003-r11s2 (regression, -8.37%): A 128 x 2-bit gshare BHT indexed by `pc[8:2] ^ ghr` with the history shifted at resolve (EX/MEM training order, ~3-4 branches stale at fetch, `ghist` snapshot carried through the fetch queue, ID/EX and EX/MEM for training) scored 240.21 vs the 262.14 r9s2 head because the proposer's own GHB sweep showed almost no cycle upside — best was GHB=1 at 4043816 cycles (-0.5% vs the 4065578 bimodal baseline) and every extra history bit only diluted the counters (GHB=7 4097085, worse than bimodal) — so the ~20-30% mispredict cut never materialised and the 128-entry flop table (256 reset flops, 128:1 read mux on `pc`, second-port RMW decode, wider queue/pipe payload) cost the ~8% Fmax (no post-change `make timing` captured, so the exact leg is unverified); global history only helps if it is speculatively updated at fetch with repair, which this front end's flop-only/redirect-free constraint forbids, so treat bigger or history-indexed BHTs as closed on this head, since the whole misprediction budget (~3% of cycles) cannot pay for any Fmax loss.

title: (slot 0 hypothesis-gen failed)

hypothesis.motivation:
After the r9s2 fetch queue the core sits within ~2-3% of the imem supply bound (about 0.78 words/cycle,
~4.07M cycles), so only Fmax can pay. In every recent run Gowin placement options 1 and 2 return the
identical Fmax and the median therefore equals them; r9s2 (106.58) and r10s0 (106.44) land on the same
value although r10s0 removed the BSRAM load-align leg and the DSP-control decode, and r10s0's own
worst-path report is then op2_0 -> cpu/u_ex/u_alu -> cpu/u_id/reg_q.op1_18 (9 cells, 14.46 ns arrival).
So the floor is the EX result -> ID forward AND-OR -> ID/EX operand D loop, launched from op2[0], which
is the LSB of both the adder and the shift amount. That loop is the one cone no earlier hypothesis
shortened: alu.sv builds three separate barrel shifters (<<, >>, >>>), two adders (+ and -), a
case(op) result mux decoded from the 5-bit alu_op flops inside EX, then ex_stage adds the
alt_sel/alt_result (JAL link, divider) mux and the `(sel_mul_lo||sel_mul_hi) ? 0` mask before
early_masked reaches the one-LUT forward AND-OR in id_stage. Those trailing selects add about 2 LUT
levels after the shifter/adder legs that a flat registered one-hot select can remove.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make the EX result network a flat AND-OR driven by one-hot result-class flags that are decoded in ID
from the FD flops (no late dependence) and registered in ID/EX ctrl (the same flop group that already
holds ctrl; they are cleared with it by flush). Classes: SUM (add/sub, one carry chain with
b ^ {32{sub}} and cin = sub, replacing the separate `a + b` and `a - b`), LOGIC (and/or/xor,
one LUT4 per bit keyed by two op bits), CMP (slt/sltu, shares the SUM chain's borrow out instead of a
third comparator), SHIFT (sll/srl/sra, below), LUI, LINK (JAL/JALR: pc+4), DIV (finished divider result)
and MUL (selects none of the early legs). early_masked then becomes OR over (class & leg) with no
case(op) behind it and no separate `alt_sel ? alt : alu_fast` mux or `sel_mul ? 0 :` mask: the MUL
class simply has all early selects low, so the existing mul_q merge on the EX/MEM output is unchanged
(early flops and mul_q stay disjoint). Shifter: replace the three barrel shifters by one right
shifter with the operand bit-reversed on the way in for SLL and on the way out (the reversals are
folded into the first and last mux stage selects, which come straight from the registered class
flags), fill bit = a[31] & is_sra. That removes about two thirds of the shifter LUTs and the
three-way shifter result merge, so op2[4:0] -> result sees 5 mux stages plus one final flat OR instead
of 5 stages plus a separate per-direction merge, then the case(op), then alt/mask.
The ALU keeps its `op` input and `out`/`fast_out` ports for test_alu.py by deriving the class flags
combinationally from `op` through a function in core_pkg.sv when no class bus is supplied (tie
cls from op inside a thin wrapper); ex_stage drives the class bus from ctrl instead, so the decode
is off the EX path in the timed netlist. The ALTOPS branch (XOR stand-ins) and the real branch
stay consistent: ALTOPS ops are mapped onto a SUM-like class with the same constants. No change
to cycles (ALU result timing and forwarding rules are untouched; late_res set is the same), so the
gain is pure Fmax on the loop that bounds options 1/2. Risk: r3s1 and r6s0 touched adjacent
cones and gave small or noisy results; the ~+1 ns hoped for on this loop only moves the median if
the other tied legs (BSRAM -> op D, FD -> fwd -> op D) are not within ~0.3 ns, which r10s0's
op2_0 -> op1_18 path being worse than its BSRAM path suggests.

changes.description: Add one-hot ALU result-class flags (res_sum, res_logic, res_cmp, res_shift, res_lui, res_link, res_div, plus sub/arith/left-shift mode bits) to ctrl_t and a decode function alu_class(op) used by test benches and the standalone alu wrapper.
Drive the new class flags from alu_op/is_jump in the existing alu_op case arms (decoder defaults stay is_illegal=1; flags default to 0).
Copy the class flags into ctrl_decoded; they register in ID/EX ctrl under the existing flush/!stall conditions (no new late term).

Add a class-bus input (derived from op when tied off for test_alu.py); implement one shared add/sub carry chain, shared slt/sltu from its borrow, a single bit-reversible right shifter with fill = a[31]&is_arith, and compute fast_out as a flat AND-OR over class flags; keep mul_lo/mul_hi and both ALTOPS and real-arithmetic branches consistent.

Feed the registered class flags to the ALU, fold LINK (pc+4) and DIV (div_result) into the same flat early_masked AND-OR, delete the alt_sel mux and the (sel_mul_lo||sel_mul_hi) mask; keep mul_q selection and the EX/MEM alu_result | mul_q merge unchanged.
Extend the vector run to cover shift edge cases (shamt 0/31, SRA of negatives, SLL/SRL via the shared shifter) and SUB/SLT/SLTU borrow cases against the shared chain.

title: Program-order dependence-distance tags computed at fetch replace ID rd-compare chains
motivation:
Cycles are within ~9% of the fetch bound (4.07M vs ~3.72M) and every backend
stall costs ~1 cycle 1:1 (r11s1: +216k bubbles = +5.3% cycles), so the only
lever left is Fmax, and the wall is a balanced set of cones that all end at
the ID/EX op1/op2 D pins or the stall_id -> fd_pop -> queue-CE net. Two of
those cones start with the same logic that is recomputed every cycle from
the FD head: 5-bit rs1/rs2 == rd compares against EX/MEM/WB producers
(fwd_select: nz, 3 equality compares, we qualifiers, youngest-wins priority,
fanout 32 -> AND-OR; the q0 -> u_fwd1 -> op1 path, 11 cells in r11s0) and the
id_ex_rd == fd_rs1/rs2 compare in hazard_unit (-> stall_id -> fd_pop -> ~260
queue flop enables). Past lessons (r4s0/r4s1) showed that moving selects
whose inputs are known a cycle early out of the data cone pays off, but the
FD word itself only arrives with the fetch, so it was never possible to
register them. In a fetch-queue front end it IS possible: whether a word's
rs1/rs2 equals the rd of its 1st/2nd/3rd PROGRAM-ORDER predecessor is a
static property of the (predicted) fetch stream and does not depend on
pipeline timing; only the mapping "predecessor k -> which pipeline stage it
sits in right now" is dynamic, and that depends only on stage valid flops.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Compute dependence-distance tags when a word is accepted into the fetch
queue and carry them in the queue entries; make fwd_select and the
load-use check combine those tags with stage-valid flops instead of
comparing register numbers in ID.

1. if_stage keeps a 3-deep history of the rd (5 bits; 0 when the word does
   not write a register: predecode opcode in {LUI,AUIPC,JAL,JALR,LOAD,OP,
   OP-IMM} and rd != 0) of the last three accepted words in program
   (fetch) order: hist1 (newest), hist2, hist3. On accept the history
   shifts and the new word's rd enters. For the accepted word w compute six
   tag bits {d1,d2,d3} x {rs1,rs2} = (w.rs == hist_k) && hist_k != 0 (use
   the history BEFORE the shift) and store them as 6 extra bits in the
   queue entry (ENT_W 65 -> 71); the tags ride q3 -> q2 -> q1 -> q0 with the
   word exactly like pred_taken. Everything is flop-launched (imem_data is
   a flop in the timed netlist, hist is flops); the compare is ~2 LUT
   levels ahead of the existing slot-write mux and sits in parallel with
   the predecode -> pred_target adder, which is deeper.
2. History repair on redirect. At the redirect cycle (redir_q = 1) the
   program-order predecessors of the redirect-cycle word are the redirecting
   instruction X (EX/MEM now) then older retired/retiring ones. Reload
   hist1 <= (X writes rd) ? X.rd : 0 (a branch has none, JAL/JALR link
   does), hist2 <= MEM/WB instruction's rd if valid && reg_write else 0,
   hist3 <= 0. Zeroing hist2/hist3 is safe: by the time the first target
   word is captured by ID/EX (>= 1 cycle after the redirect) anything older
   than X has already written the regfile. The word fetched in the redirect
   cycle gets its tags from this repaired history (compare against the
   repaired values, not the stale ones). A predicted-taken JAL/branch needs
   no repair: fetch order is the dynamic order and the JAL is hist1.
3. fwd_select / id_stage: the three in-flight producers are exactly the
   last valid instructions in EX, MEM, WB, in that order (valid instructions
   in those stages are in program order and the oldest has retired into the
   regfile). Define from flops: v_ex = ID/EX.valid && ex_we (non-late
   reg_write; a late producer stalls the consumer instead), v_mem =
   EX/MEM.valid && mem_we_nxt, v_wb = wb_we. Let n_ex, n_mem, n_wb be the
   VALID-instruction (not reg_write) flags of the three stages; predecessor
   k maps to the k-th valid stage counting EX, MEM, WB. The tag bits d1..d3
   already include "predecessor writes this rs", so
      sel_ex      = tag at the position mapped to EX
      sel_mem_*   = tag at the position mapped to MEM (split ld/alu by
                    EX/MEM.mem_to_reg as today)
      sel_wb      = tag at the position mapped to WB
      sel_ram     = none of the above
   with youngest-wins priority resolved by the ordering of the tag bits
   (d1 beats d2 beats d3: tag d1 for rs1 means predecessor 1 is the nearest
   producer -> pick it regardless of which stage it is in). The position
   mapping is a handful of LUT4 over {n_ex, n_mem, n_wb} flops. Note that a
   producer that is not a writer contributes a zero in the history, so the
   tags are only set for true register producers; but the history must still
   advance for every accepted word so that distance counting stays aligned
   with the stage-valid ordering. Misaligned-trap squashed writers
   (mem_we_nxt = 0 after trap clearing) must make the select fall through to
   the next-older tag: keep the final AND with the stage reg_write flag (a
   1-LUT AND, not a compare).
4. hazard_unit load-use: load_use = id_ex_late_res && (d1_rs1 || d1_rs2)
   of the FD head (q0 tag) -- ID/EX holding a bubble has late_res = 0 and
   v = 0 so a stale tag cannot stall. This removes the 5-bit equality chain
   from stall_id -> fd_pop -> queue enables.
5. Wrong-path words are flushed with the queue (qv clears on redirect), so
   tags on killed entries never reach ID. Stalls/holds never change tags
   (they are properties of the word + program order), and the sources are
   re-evaluated every cycle the consumer waits in ID, as today.

cones lose ~2 LUT levels (compare + we/priority), the SAME cycle count
(decode/forward semantics are identical, only the select computation is
retimed into fetch). Risk: ~+24 FF and a few LUTs in if_stage; the redirect
history reload adds a small mux onto hist flops only. To be safe the
implementer should add a cosim/formal-equivalent debug assertion (sim only)
that the new tag-derived selects equal the old compare-derived selects every
cycle, then delete the old logic.

title: Loop-stream predictor: rolling 16-word window replays straight-line backward-taken loops without imem, flop-only control
motivation:
Measured on this head (cosim, --istall --dstall, 4065578 bench cycles, 2.92M retired
instructions, IPC 0.72 vs the 0.78 words/cycle imem delivers): branch-direction accuracy
has no cycle leverage left. A 64-entry XOR-folded BHT cuts mispredicts 56k -> 42k yet
saves only 7.4k cycles (-0.18%) because the 4-deep fetch queue already hides most of the
redirect penalty, so even a perfect direction predictor is worth < 1%. RAS (r7s2) and
gshare (r11s2) confirmed this. What the queue cannot hide is that fetch itself is the
bound: imem accepts only ~78% of cycles. An offline trace of the CoreMark run shows 42%
of dynamic instructions execute inside straight-line backward-taken loops of <= 16 words
(27% for <= 8) - crc, matrix, list and state-machine inner loops - i.e. the same words are
refetched through the stalling imem bus over and over. The r10s2 L0 cache (-11% cycles)
proved the cycle upside of bypassing imem stalls but died on Fmax because it put a
pc-indexed LUT-RAM lookup + tag compare ahead of accept/predecode. A loop-stream buffer
driven by the branch predictor needs neither: no address-indexed lookup, no tag, all
control on flops.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a loop-stream window to if_stage. (1) A 16 x 32-bit flop shift register S (newest at
S[15]) shifts in every accepted word (CE = accept, already flop-only: imem_ready &&
!qv[3]); a 5-bit saturating `seq_cnt` flop counts consecutive sequentially delivered words
(cleared on pred_taken accept or redirect). (2) Detect at accept: pred_taken && backward
(imem_data[31]) && n = (pc - pred_target)/4 + 1 <= 16 (the distance is just the sign-
extended low offset bits of the already predecoded imm_b/imm_j, no extra adder) &&
seq_cnt >= n-1. Then S already holds the loop body T..B once the branch word shifts in;
set `replay` and a one-hot head select hsel = 16-n (flops). (3) While `replay` (and not
`redirect`), the delivered word is S[hsel] (keep a pre-read `head_q` flop so the extra
logic ahead of predecode is a single flop-selected 2:1 LUT), accept = !qv[3] (imem_ready
ignored), and the word re-enters S[15] so the ring rotates; pc keeps advancing through the
existing predecode/pred_target path (imem_addr is simply ignored). pc/pred_taken/BHT
logic is untouched. Replay ends (replay <= 0, next word comes from imem at the already
correct pc) when: the delivered word at the last position is not predicted taken, any
earlier body word is predicted taken, or `redirect` fires (the loop-exit mispredict
flushes the queue exactly like today, with the redirect-cycle word coming from imem).
Retired state, rvfi_insn and pc come from the delivered word, so the backend, hazard
unit and RVFI are untouched; formal sees an ordinary fetch stream (a symbolic imem is
just not consulted during replay). Expected: replayed loops run at the backend-bound rate
instead of 0.78 words/cycle; with ~35-42% of instructions eligible and a backend floor
of ~1.2 cycles/instr (r10s2 ideal-fetch run: 3.61M cycles) the cycle gain is ~4-7%.
Fmax must stay flat: S adds ~530 flops with CE = accept (same cone as q0..q3), one
flop-selected LUT before predecode; nothing is added to redirect_raw, the EX cones or
the BSRAM/DSP/forward walls. If the extra mux shows on the predecode -> pc D leg, the
implementer should register the replay word's predecode (is_jal/is_br/imm) in the window
instead of muxing raw words. Do not size beyond 16 words (trace shows no gain at 32).

title: Flop-only stall cone: predecoded is_div + done flop for ex_busy, and ID/EX data-flop CE decoupled from the load-use compare
motivation:
Cycles are within ~5% of the fetch-bandwidth floor (4.07M cycles; ~22% imem stalls
cap fetch at 0.78 word/cycle), so only Fmax can pay for a >4.6% gain; every recent
CPI/predictor/fetch change either lost to Fmax (r10s2, r11s2, r12s1, r12s2) or was flat.
The stall/hold cone is still deep for what it fans out to: ex_busy is a 5-bit alu_op
compare (4-way) AND valid AND !redir_q AND (divider state == DONE, a 3-bit decode),
OR-ed with the load-use compare (5-bit rd == rs1/rs2, late_res) and dmem_stall into
stall_id, which is the CE of every ID/EX data flop (op1/op2/imm/pc/rd, ~200 timed flops)
plus ctrl, the fetch-queue pop shift (~200 flops) and the EX/MEM clear arm
(`ex_busy || redir_q`). Earlier fixes took `redirect` and the DSP controls out of
these cones but ex_busy and the load-use compare are still in the CE of the whole ID/EX
data register, where they only need to be there for dmem_stall and the divide.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Three IPC-neutral edits that make the hold/stall nets flop-driven and cut fanout:
(1) Predecode is_div (alu_op in DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU) in ID into ctrl_t (like late_res),
and make the divider's DONE a dedicated flop (done_q: set entering S_DONE, cleared on
advance/reset; identical cycle behaviour to state==S_DONE). ex_busy then becomes one
LUT4 of flops: in.valid & ctrl.is_div & !redir_q & !done_q (is_div_op gating of the
divider start and the wrong-path squash is preserved). This removes ~2 LUT levels from
ex_busy, which feeds stall_id, flush_id, stall of the divider advance, the EX/MEM
bubble arm and mul_q.
(2) Split the ID/EX register enables. The ctrl/valid/pred_taken flops keep the full
`reset||flush` / `!stall_id` behaviour. The data flops (pc, op1, op2, rv1, rv2, imm, rd,
rs addrs, instr) load on a new `!hold_id` where hold_id = dmem_stall || ex_busy
(flop/LUT2-fed, exported by hazard_unit) instead of stall_id. On a load-use bubble
flush_id already clears ctrl/valid/pred_taken so the data fields of the bubble are dead
(same argument the file already makes for flush/redirect), and the FD head is not
popped, so the next cycle recomputes op1/op2 from the same instruction with the newly
available MEM-now forward term. This drops the load-use register-number compare out of
the CE cone of ~200 data flops (it still drives flush_id, fd_pop and the ~30 ctrl CE).
(3) In ex_stage, restrict the `ex_busy || redir_q` bubble arm of the EX/MEM register to
ctrl, valid and branch_taken (the fields consulted when valid = 0: reg_write, mem_read,
mem_write, is_branch, is_illegal) and let the data fields (alu_result, mem_addr,
write_data, rd, pc_next, rs*_val, instr) load on !stall alone, mirroring the existing
ID/EX treatment; mul_q keeps its clear so alu_result | mul_q stays exact for valid
non-MUL ops (both are rewritten every advancing cycle). A bubble never forwards
(mem_we = reg_write = 0), never retires (valid = 0), and never writes dmem
(mem_write = 0), so the stale data is unobservable.
Cycle count must be identical to the 4065578 baseline (no new stall, no new bubble);
the gain is purely Fmax from shallower/lighter hold, CE and squash nets, expected to
help the tied compare->redir_q, EX-result->operand and BSRAM->operand legs by relieving
routing congestion around the shared stall/CE nets. Must keep the RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS
branch (is_div_op = 0, ex_busy = 0) intact and re-run cosim, formal and test_alu.py.

title: Slim the two tied forward legs structurally: word-only raw load forward + shifter on its own late registers
motivation:
Fresh make timing on the r9s2 head (place option 0, 92.3 MHz) shows the wall is two
families within 0.08 ns: (1) dmem BSRAM DO -> mem_stage byte shift -> sign/zero-extend
select (fanout 9 then 16) -> mem_ld_val -> id_stage forward AND-OR -> op1/op2 D, 9 LUTs
with ~5.4 ns of the 10.8 ns data path being routing; (2) ID/EX alu_op flop -> ALU 11-way
fast_out case (barrel shifter + adder + logic) -> alt/mask mux -> EX/MEM.alu_result,
7 LUTs. Queue-depth data says cycles are saturated: r8s2 (FD+2) ran 4,086,552 cycles and
r9s2 (FD+3) 4,065,578, so r9s2's gain over r8s2 was Fmax, not stall hiding, and a deeper
queue is dead. The fluid fetch-bound model (imem 0.78 word/cycle -> ~3.72M cycle floor vs
~3.4M of backend work) leaves roughly 10% backend slack, so a small number of rare
one-cycle consumer stalls should be nearly free while removing logic from both tied legs.
Prior LUT-level reshuffles (r10s0 fused lane select; r6s0 cofactor muxes) kept every
producer one-cycle and so left the byte shift or the shifter on the leg; this removes them.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
(a) Loads: classify word loads (LW) as the only load class whose dmem_rdata is forwarded
from MEM-now. The forward term sel_mem_ld becomes ({32{s_mld_word}} & dmem_rdata) with no
shift or extension, so BSRAM DO -> AND-OR -> op D is ~3 LUTs instead of 9. Sub-word loads
(LB/LBU/LH/LHU, a small fraction of CoreMark loads) get a new ctrl bit late2 so the
hazard unit stalls their consumer through both the EX and MEM cycles; the consumer then
takes the value from the existing WB-now term (wb_val = registered, already aligned
read_data), which is flop-launched. The align/sign-extend cone stays only on the MEM/WB
read_data D pin, which has no forward fan-out behind it.
(b) Shifts: SLL/SRL/SRA(+I) are moved out of alu.sv fast_out into a separate shifter whose
result is registered in its own EX/MEM flop set sh_q (zero for non-shift, squashed like
mul_q) and OR-merged with alu_result/mul_q after the flop, exactly the mul_q pattern that
won in r3s0. Shifts are marked late_res, so only the immediate consumer waits one cycle and
takes the value from the MEM-now alu term. fast_out loses its deepest mux input, and the
early_result/alt mux cone feeding alu_result and the EX-now forward shrinks.
Expected cycle cost is ~1% (immediate consumers of shifts and byte/half loads, absorbed
largely by the fetch-bound slack and the 4-entry queue); expected Fmax gain is the point:
both tied families lose 3-4 LUT levels together, which is what prior single-family tweaks
lacked.

title: Small ring-buffer loop predictor: replay recorded loop body into the fetch queue with a fixed head tap, imem path untouched
motivation:
On the r9s2 head the core is fetch-supply bound, not predictor bound: 4,065,578 cycles
against a floor of roughly instr/0.78 (22% imem stalls) leaves only ~5% above the floor,
and the whole mispredict budget is ~3.3% of cycles (~70k redirects x 2 bubbles), so bigger
BHTs, gshare (r11s2), a RAS (r7s2) and L0 caches (r10s2) were all closed. The one lever that
measurably breaks the 0.78 words/cycle floor is replaying a loop body from flops instead of
the stalling imem bus: r12s2 (rolling 16-word loop-stream window) cut cycles 4,065,578 ->
3,871,777 (-4.77%) but scored 258.81 because Fmax fell 106.6 -> 100.2 MHz. Its timing report
names the ALU carry chain (op2 -> u_alu -> alu_result, 37 cells), i.e. NOT a loop-buffer leg:
the loss came from +581 LUT4 / +574 FF of area (4473 / 2601 vs 3892 / 2027) degrading the
placement of the tied EX wall, plus the 16:1 head AND-OR and the `dw = rp ? head_q : imem_data`
mux in front of predecode. A cheaper structure with the same cycle win is the fitness lever:
-4.8% cycles at unchanged Fmax is ~+5%, just over the 4.6% bar.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the rolling window with a RECORD-then-REPLAY ring (a loop predictor in the classic
sense: the BHT-trained backward-taken branch is the trigger) with three cost cuts versus r12s2.

1. Trigger / recording. When fetch accepts a conditional backward branch that the BHT predicts
   taken and whose offset is >= -(RING-1)*4 (RING = 8 words, not 16; offset known from
   imm_b, already predecoded), latch loop_tgt = pred_target and loop_br_pc = pc, clear a
   2-bit `rec_state`, and RECORD the next iteration: every word accepted from loop_tgt up to
   and including the branch is written into ring[wptr] (wptr increments per accepted word;
   write is a per-entry CE decode of wptr, imem_data is just an extra D input on 8 x 33 flops).
   Abort (rec_state <= IDLE) if a different taken prediction, a redirect, or an overflow
   (>RING words) occurs before the branch is seen again. Bodies that contain an inner
   predicted-taken branch other than the loop-back are simply not recorded (straight-line
   bodies only; inner not-taken-predicted branches are fine and are re-verified in EX as usual).
2. Replay via a ring with a FIXED head tap (no read mux). Once the loop-back branch has been
   recorded, ring length L = number of words is known. On the next predicted-taken loop-back
   the front end enters REPLAY: each cycle (not gated by imem_ready) a word is offered to the
   fetch queue from ring[0]; on consumption the ring ROTATES (ring[i] <= ring[i+1], the old
   head is re-inserted at ring[L-1] via the same per-entry write-decode used for recording).
   The head is therefore always ring[0]: no 8:1 AND-OR read mux on the queue write path. The
   replay word's pred_taken (1 only for the loop-back branch itself, stored as a 33rd bit per
   entry at record time) is stored with the word, so replay needs NO predecode and the
   imem_data -> predecode -> pred_target adder -> pc D leg and the queue-slot D inputs
   keep exactly the r9s2 logic (the replay value enters as one extra AND-OR term on the
   queue-slot word w, only on the instr/pred bits; imem_data is not muxed ahead of predecode).
   The queue word's pc comes from a 30-bit `rpc` counter (rpc <= loop_tgt on loop entry/wrap,
   else rpc+4) held in flops; the fetch `pc` register is NOT advanced during replay and is
   loaded at replay exit with the fall-through address `loop_br_pc + 4`.
3. Exit / safety. The queue's existing `accept` gate (`!qv[3]`) still throttles replay, so
   the queue never overflows. Replay ends when the loop-back branch, replayed with
   pred_taken=1, mispredicts: EX already raises the normal registered `redirect` for
   pred_taken ^ actual_taken, which flushes the queue, sets pc <= redirect_target and resets
   rec_state/replay to IDLE (one extra flop term, no new EX logic). So the exit costs the
   same 2 bubbles a normal loop-exit mispredict costs today, and every replayed instruction is
   verified by the unchanged EX/BHT machinery. CoreMark code is never written, so no
   store-snoop invalidation is needed; rec_state is cleared on every `redirect` to stay
   safe. RVFI order/pc continuity is unchanged
   because instructions reach ID with the same pc/instr/pred_taken a real fetch would have
   produced.

Expected effect: instructions in <=8-word straight-line loops (CoreMark crc bit loops,
matrix inner loops, list walks) are supplied at 1 word/cycle instead of 0.78, saving the
~22% imem stall share on those fetches. r12s2 measured -4.77% cycles with a 16-word
window; an 8-word ring keeps most of that (loops <=8 words dominate the inner-loop mix)
at ~1/2 the flops (~8 x 33 = 264 vs ~530) and without the head read mux, which is what
should keep the area/placement of the tied EX / BSRAM-load walls at the r9s2 level.
Verification plan: run cosim for cycle count first (accept only if cycles <= ~3.90M), then
`make timing` and compare the worst path / LUT4 / FF against the r9s2 head (3892 / 2027);
if LUT4 grows by more than ~300 shrink RING to 6 or drop the ring write-decode sharing.
Do not touch the imem_data -> predecode -> pc/queue-D cone, ex_stage, id_stage or the DSP /
load-align / forward paths.

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-003-r13s2 (regression, -4.63%): An 8-word record-then-replay loop ring (fixed `ring[0]` head tap with rotate-on-consume, 3-state FSM armed by a predicted-taken backward branch decoded from raw `imem_data`, `accept = !qv[3] && (rp || imem_ready)`) scored 249.99 vs the 262.14 r9s2 head — worse than the 16-word, read-mux r12s2 window (258.81) despite ~half the flops and no head AND-OR, so r12s2's "area and the 16:1 read mux caused the Fmax loss" diagnosis was wrong and shrinking the buffer does not fix a loop-buffer family — the replay word still enters every queue slot as a third `imem_data`/`rhead`/shift term in the q0..q3 payload mux (`ins_f`/`ins_r` split), `rp` joins the `accept`/`ins`/pc-CE cone, and the trigger decodes `imem_data` -> FSM D, i.e. the cost sits in the insertion point on the fetch wall, not in the storage (no post-change cycle count or `make timing` was captured, so how much of the miss is smaller cycle savings from straight-line <=8-word bodies and a record iteration vs Fmax is unverified) — two loop-buffer attempts (r12s2, r13s2) now lost, so treat loop/trace replay as closed on this head unless the replay word is injected downstream of the queue (e.g. a separate flop-only mux at the FD head) with a measured timing report showing the fetch wall unchanged.

title: Take control decode off the tied Fmax cones: registered DSP-sign/is_div/ALU-select flops and a priority-free EX forward term
motivation:
I ran `make timing` on the r9s2 head with all three placement options (the evaluator
scores the median). Options 1 and 2 both give 106.577 MHz with the SAME top-25 list, all
within 0.06 ns of 14.68 ns arrival (slack -4.32..-4.38 on the 5 ns SDC clock):
  * ID/EX.alu_op_4 -> n225 (decode op==MULH/MULHSU) -> alu.mul_a_32 (a[31]&mul_sa) -> DSP
    (3.76 ns) -> 2 LUT -> mul_q: 3 of the top 5 and ~10 of the top 25 paths. The decode
    LUT + the 1.4 ns alu_op route + the extra ext-bit LUT are ~1.8 ns that a flop could remove.
  * ID/EX.rd_3 -> fwd_select `ex_rd == a` (mapped onto Gowin carry-chain ALU cells, 0.55 ns
    + 1.4 ns route) -> 3 LUTs of `!m_ex && ...` priority masking (fanout-32 select net)
    -> 3-LUT forward AND-OR -> op1/op2 D: 9 cells, top-5 and ~6 of the top 25.
  * ID/EX.alu_op_4 -> is_div_op -> ex_busy -> stall_id -> fd_pop -> queue q2 CE (paths 12, 15).
  * dmem BSRAM DO -> load align -> forward AND-OR -> op D (paths 7, 10, 21, 23, 25).
  * op1 -> ALU legs -> alu_result D (paths 6, 18, ALU result mux selected by the 5-bit alu_op).
Placement option 0 (92.3 MHz) shows the same families, plus mem_addr[1:0] -> misalign ->
mem_we_nxt (fanout 32 select) -> op D and alu_op_3 -> 6-level result mux -> alu_result.
Each past single-family tweak (r9s0, r10s0, r10s1, r13s0, r13s1) was flat or negative
because the other families sit within 0.1 ns; r9s0's DSP+load predecode won +8% when it
hit several families at once. Every family above has one thing in common: a 5-bit
encoded field (alu_op, rd compare, mem_addr[1:0]/width) is decoded into a select inside
the timed cone one cycle after it could have been decoded for free.
