hypothesis.hypothesis:
One micro-architectural theme, no change to cycle count or pipeline structure: move the
control decode that sits on the measured tied paths into flops that are loaded from the
decoder / EX one cycle earlier, and take the EX-forward priority off the select cone.
1. DSP controls (hits the 3-of-5 DSP paths): decoder/id_stage add ctrl bits mul_sa,
   mul_sb, sel_mul_lo, sel_mul_hi (one-hot, registered in ID/EX). alu.sv gets them as
   ports (keep the op-decoded behaviour under a parameter so test_alu.py still passes) so
   mul_a[32]/mul_b[32] = op[31] & flop and the lo/hi merge selects are flops (DSP -> 1 LUT
   -> mul_q). Drop the `ex_busy || redir_q` clear on mul_q (bubbles have valid=0 and
   reg_write=0, and mul_q only reaches consumers qualified by reg_write).
2. Priority-free EX forward (hits the rd_3 -> fwd_select -> op D paths): in fwd_select
   the mem/wb/regfile/pc-imm selects no longer contain `!m_ex`; only ex_rd==a (m_ex,
   computed with a plain LUT AND of registered ex_we/nz, not a carry-chain compare - write
   it as an XOR/OR reduction) remains, and id_stage ends with one LUT:
   op_d = E ? ex_val : base, E = m_ex && !use_const, base = AND-OR of the one-hot
   {mem_ld, mem_alu, wb, ram, pc|imm} terms (use_pc/use_imm folded into those selects as
   early FD-flop terms). ex_val and mem_ld_val each see one LUT level after the
   alu/BSRAM-launched data instead of three.
3. is_div / ALU result select flops: ctrl.is_div replaces the 4-way alu_op compare in
   is_div_op (ex_busy = flop && !div_done, valid && !redir_q kept) - do NOT split the
   ID/EX or EX/MEM CE/clear nets (that was r13s0's failure); and a one-hot ALU result
   class (sel_add, sel_sub, sel_and, sel_or, sel_xor, sel_slt, sel_sltu, sel_sll, sel_srl,
   sel_sra, sel_lui) registered in ID/EX drives a flat AND-OR for alu_fast instead of the
   5-bit case.
4. Memory misalign trap decided in EX (small): jalr_sum[1:0] + width give `mis` in EX;
   ctrl_with_trap in ex_stage clears reg_write / sets is_illegal for loads/stores too, so
   mem_stage reg_write_nxt is just in.ctrl.reg_write (a flop) and the mem_addr[1:0]
   -> misalign -> mem_we_nxt -> fanout-32 select leg disappears. dmem_wen/ren gating and
   RVFI rmask/wmask keep the exact same values (misalign gates them as before).
Expected effect: removes 1-3 LUT levels/1-2 ns of routing from each of the top families;
because they all move together the median wall should lift from ~9.4 ns to ~8.9 ns of
data delay (~+5% Fmax). Cycle count must stay at 4065578 (no scheduling change). Check
`make timing TARGET=bench --all-options` style output (all 3 options) before/after, not
option 0 only. If the ALU data legs (op1 -> shifter/adder -> alu_result, also at
14.6 ns in option 1) become the sole wall, report that so the next round targets the
shifter.

title: Flat EX forward network: one-hot ALU result classes in ID/EX, link/div/mul terms taken off the ex-now forward loop
motivation:
Cycles sit within ~5-8% of the fetch-supply floor (4,065,578 cycles; ~22% imem
stalls cap fetch at 0.78 word/cycle), so only Fmax can pay for a >4.6% win. The
log shows what sets the median Fmax of the r9s2 head. r9s2 seeds were
[92.3, 106.6, 106.6]: seed 0 is the BSRAM -> load-align -> forward AND-OR -> op D
leg (9 cells). r10s0 fused that leg to ~2 levels and seed 0 rose to 109.1, but the
median stayed at 106.4 because seeds 1/2 sat on the other tied family, which its
own report names: ID/EX op2 flop -> cpu/u_ex/u_alu -> id_stage op1 D (9 cells,
arrival 14.46 ns). That is the ex-now back-to-back-ALU loop: op flops -> adder /
logic / shifter -> 11-way `case(op)` -> `alt_sel` mux (jump link / divider result)
-> `sel_mul_*` zero mask -> `early_masked` == `fwd_val` -> forward AND-OR -> op D.
None of the three mux stages behind the adder is needed by the forwarded value:
JAL/JALR and MUL* are `late_res` (never forwarded from EX), and the divider result
is only forwarded because DIV is not `late_res`. Yet all three sit on the loop. The
`case(op)` also re-decodes the 5-bit alu_op after the ID/EX flop on every bit.
This is the one tied family not yet attacked on the current head; earlier LUT-depth
reshuffles hit the BSRAM, DSP and reg_write cones (r9s0, r10s0, r10s1), and the
class-predecode that paid off in r3s1 predates the end-of-ID forwarding.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Give the EX forward value its own flat, flop-select-driven network and keep the
rare, late terms only on the EX/MEM capture leg.

1. Predecode the ALU result class in id_stage into one-hot ctrl_t flops (derived
   from dec_alu_op, so decoder.sv and its unit tests are untouched):
   k_add (ADD/SUB/loads/stores/AUIPC/JAL address ops, with a `sub` flag so one
   add/sub chain serves both), k_log + lop[1:0] (AND/OR/XOR; LUI passes op2 as
   a logic "pass-b"), k_shl / k_shr (+ `arith` flag for SRA), k_slt (+ `uns` flag),
   k_alt (JAL/JALR link or finished divide). MUL* classes are all-zero, so a
   multiplier op reads 0 from the early network without any mask.
2. In ex_stage build `fwd_val` as a flat one-hot AND-OR of the class results only
   (sum, logic, shift, slt): the select inputs come straight from flops, so there
   is no alu_op decode, no `alt_sel` mux and no `sel_mul_*` mask after the
   adder/shifter. The EX/MEM.alu_result flop D becomes
   `fwd_val | ({32{k_alt}} & alt_result)` (classes are one-hot, so k_alt ops see
   fwd_val == 0). That extra OR sits only on the flop D leg, which ends at a pin
   and has one LUT of slack relative to the loop that continues through the
   forward AND-OR into op D.
3. Mark DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU `late_res` in id_stage (consumer waits one cycle and
   takes the result from the MEM-now alu_result term, exactly like MUL*). CoreMark's
   timed region has no divides and a divide already costs ~36 cycles, so CPI is
   unchanged. This lets the divider result and `is_div_op` (4 alu_op compares &
   valid & !redir_q) leave the forwarded value completely.

   OR them in through a predecoded k_m flag, so riscv-formal still exercises the
   new network for every base-ISA op. alu.sv keeps its `op`-driven interface and
   `out` for test_alu.py; the DSP product path and `mul_q` are left exactly as
   they are (r10s1 showed that touching them lowers Fmax).

9 cells to <=7 and name the next worst leg; r10s0 shows the next walls sit at

title: FD-head loop replay: window fed from q0 pops, trigger from q0 flops, replay injected only into q0 (fetch wall untouched)
motivation:
Measured numbers from earlier rounds on this head: 4.07M cycles, 2.92M retired instructions,
IPC 0.72 against the 0.78 words/cycle that imem accepts. The core is fetch-bound. Every
direction/target predictor variant is already closed: perfect direction prediction is worth
<1% of cycles (a 64-entry BHT cut mispredicts 56k->42k and saved only 7.4k cycles), the RAS
ceiling is 0.64%, and gshare found no usable history signal. The only front-end change with
measured cycle upside is supplying instructions without going through the stalling imem bus:
r12s2 (16-word loop window) cut cycles 4.8% (4065578 -> 3871777) and r13s2 (8-word ring)
cut 2.5%. Both lost fitness (258.81, 249.99 vs 262.14) because they put the replay word
on the fetch wall: a 2:1 mux ahead of predecode/pred_target (r12s2), or a third source into
every queue slot payload mux, `rp` in the accept/ins/pc-CE cone, and a trigger decoded from
imem_data into an FSM D pin (r13s2). LESSONS.md leaves exactly one retry open: inject the
replay word downstream of the queue, at the FD head, with a flop-only mux, and leave
imem_data -> predecode -> pc/queue D untouched. This hypothesis is that retry.

hypothesis.motivation:

measured cycle upside is supplying instructions without going through the stalling imem bus:
r12s2 (16-word loop window) cut cycles 4.8% (4065578 -> 3871777) and r13s2 (8-word ring)
cut 2.5%. Both lost fitness (258.81, 249.99 vs 262.14) because they put the replay word
on the fetch wall: a 2:1 mux ahead of predecode/pred_target (r12s2), or a third source into
every queue slot payload mux, `rp` in the accept/ins/pc-CE cone, and a trigger decoded from
imem_data into an FSM D pin (r13s2). LESSONS.md leaves exactly one retry open: inject the

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Edit only if_stage.sv. The imem_data -> predecode -> pred_target -> pc D path, the BHT, the
w = {pc, imem_data, pred_taken} word and the q1..q3 payload muxes stay byte-identical.

1. Window (record, flop -> flop). A shift register win[0..N-1] (N = 16 words, or 8 if area
   or timing demands) of {instr[31:0], pred_taken}. It shifts in q0 whenever q0 is consumed:
   `pop && qv[0]`. There is no mux from imem_data and no new fetch-side load. Alongside it
   keep a `run` counter (saturating, 5 bits) = number of consecutive straight-line words
   just popped. `run` is cleared on redirect, and set to 0 after popping a pred_taken word
   (JAL or predicted-taken branch). Otherwise it increments on each valid pop.

2. Trigger (from q0 flops only, never from imem_data). When q0 holds a valid conditional
   branch (opcode 1100011) with pred_taken = 1 and a short backward offset,
   {instr[31], instr[7], instr[30:25]} == 8'hFF, the body length is L = 9 - instr[11:9] words
   (4..32 bytes back). Extend the offset check to -4*(N-1) for N = 16. If run >= L-1 on the
   pop of that branch, the L-1 body words before it are contiguous and win[L-2] is the loop
   head. Set the flop `armed <= 1`, with the hit length L-1 in a small `lb_len` register.
   `armed` is cleared on redirect or if a later pop breaks the condition. The trigger is a
   flop-to-flop cone into one flop.

3. Replay entry and steady state. While `armed` (or `rp`) and q0 is valid, the q0 D mux
   gets one extra source R, selected by the flop-only `sel_r = rp | (armed & qv[0])`:
     q0 <= redirect ? {redirect_target, imem_data, 0}   (unchanged, wins)
         : sel_r    ? R
         : ins[0]   ? w
         : pop      ? q1 : q0
   with R = { pc_r, win[lb_len-1 .. i.e. L-2], pred_bit } loaded only when `pop` is 1.
   The tap index depends only on `lb_len` flops, so it is a flop-selected AND-OR
   (<= 2 LUT levels) and `pop` stays a CE. Because the window shifts on every pop, the
   tap index is constant: c(t+1) = win[L-2] with q0 = c(t) and win[0] = c(t-1). So the
   window rotates the loop body through itself with no pointer arithmetic.
   pc_r = q0.pred_taken ? q0.pc + imm_b(q0.instr) : q0.pc + 4, a single 30-bit adder from
   q0 flops (same shape as the existing pred_target adder). pred_bit comes from the
   recorded window bit.
   On the first pop with `armed`: set rp <= 1, force qv <= 4'b0001 (flush q1..q3) and drop
   any word accepted that cycle.

4. Fetch pause. accept = imem_ready && !qv[3] && !rp. `rp` is a flop, so accept stays
   flop-only. pc is irrelevant during replay and holds.

5. Exit. The loop exit is an ordinary mispredict: the recorded back-edge carries
   pred_taken = 1, EX compares it against the real outcome, and redir_q fires. Redirect
   clears rp, armed and run, refills FD from redirect_target as today, and restarts
   fetch (pc <= redirect_target + 4). Any other mid-body redirect exits the same way. No
   change to ex_stage.sv, hazard_unit.sv, rvfi or the BHT. Replayed words carry the same
   instr/pc/pred_taken as a refetch, so RVFI order, pc_wdata and the trap checks are
   unaffected, and a replayed back-edge trains the BHT through the existing EX/MEM port.

Expected effect: the straight-line loops of <= 16 words (about 42% of dynamic instructions
in the earlier offline trace; r12s2 realised -4.8% cycles) stop paying the 22% imem stall
and run at backend speed. This design differs from r12s2/r13s2 in four ways. The replay
word never touches imem_data or predecode. Nothing is added to the q1..q3 payload muxes.
`accept` gains only a flop input. The trigger decodes q0 flops, not the raw fetched word.
Area is about +530 FF for N = 16, or +270 for N = 8.

Verification the implementer MUST do: run `make timing` on the head and on the candidate
and confirm that imem_data -> pc/queue D and q0 -> ID decode slack did not move. If the
q0 D mux or the trigger cone becomes the new worst path, drop N to 8, or register the
trigger one more cycle (arm one word later). Cosim cycle count should drop toward
~3.87M. Run the riscv-formal single-issue checks (the replayed word must satisfy the
pc_fwd / insn checks like any fetched word).

Add the 16-word (or 8) {instr, pred_taken} window shifted on q0 pops, the straight-line `run` counter, the q0-flop back-edge trigger (armed / lb_len), the flop-selected replay source R into the q0 D mux only, the pc_r adder from q0 flops, and the `rp` fetch-pause term in accept; clear all replay state on redirect/reset. imem_data -> predecode -> pc and q1..q3 payload muxes stay unchanged.

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-003-r14s2 (regression, -5.11%): The FD-head loop replay that r13s2 left as the one open retry (16 x 33 flop window shifted by `pop && qv[0]`, trigger decoded from q0 flops only, replay word `{q0.pc + imm/4, win_q[tap]}` injected as a third `sel_r` source of the q0 D mux, `accept` gaining only `!rp`, `imem_data` -> predecode -> pc/queue D byte-identical) still scored 248.75 vs the 262.14 r9s2 head, about as bad as the fetch-wall designs (r12s2 -1.27%, r13s2 -4.63%) — so keeping the replay word off the fetch wall is not what makes a loop buffer free, and the r13s2 diagnosis that "the cost sits in the insertion point on the fetch wall" was at best partial; the new load sits on the backend side instead: the stall-derived `pop` (load-use/dmem_stall/ex_busy cone) now drives ~530 window CE pins plus the `sel_r` q0 mux select and the `qv` D arm, and q0 -> 30-bit replay adder / 16:1 tap AND-OR / `run + off_idx` trigger adder add cones behind the q0 flops that also feed ID decode (no post-change cycle count or `make timing` was captured, so how much is Fmax vs smaller-than-3.87M cycle savings is unverified) — three loop-replay variants have now lost 1-5%, so treat loop/trace replay as closed on this head; any future fetch-supply idea must bring a measured path report for `pop` fanout and q0 -> ID legs, not just an argument that `imem_data` is untouched.

title: Clean the forward-network inputs: flat DO->op AND-OR for loads, no link/div term on fwd_val, DSP ext-bit flops, replicated regfile address flops
motivation:
I ran `make timing --all-options --paths 25` on the r14s0 head (4,065,578 cycles, so IPC is at the fetch
floor and only Fmax can pay for the 4.6% bar). Options 1 and 2 both give 112.419 MHz (this is the median);
option 0 gives 98.461. In option 1 the top 25 paths sit in 14.04..14.19 ns arrival and every one of them ends
at an ID/EX op1/op2 D pin or at mul_q/redir_q. The .tr shows what each family actually spends:
  1. dmem BSRAM DO (tC2Q 2.26 ns, vs 0.23 for a flop) -> shifted_7 (2 LUTs) -> mem_ld_val (3 LUTs, the sign
     bit fans out to 18-24 loads) -> op2_d (2 LUTs): 12 of the top 25 paths, 7 LUT levels after the BSRAM.
     The lane/width/sext selects are known from flops long before DO arrives, but the RTL builds them as a
     `>> (addr*8)` barrel shift followed by a width/sext case, so the data bits walk through all the levels.
  2. op flops -> adder/logic/shift -> `alu_fast` AND-OR -> `early_masked` OR (link, divider) -> forward
     AND-OR -> op D: 8-10 cells (paths 2, 4).
  3. ID/EX.pc_3 -> pc+4 carry -> `early_masked` (is_jump & pc+4 term) -> ex_val -> op1 D (path 5, 6 cells,
     5.99 ns of routing). This one is a FALSE path: JAL/JALR are late_res, ctrl.ex_fwd is 0 for them, so the
     link term can never reach an operand through ex_val, but STA cannot know that and the pc+4 incrementer
     sits on the forward cone.
  4. op1_31 -> `mul_a_32 = a[31] & mul_sa` LUT (1.7 ns route in) -> DSP (3.76) -> mul_result LUT -> mul_q
     (paths 7, 19-23).
  5. q0 rs1/rs2 flops -> regfile 32:1 read mux select, 4.8 ns on ONE net (path 13, 4 cells): each address
     bit drives ~16 mux cells x 32 data bits.
Single-family fixes on earlier heads were flat (r10s0, r14s1) because all of these are tied within 0.15 ns;
r14s0 moved the wall by cutting a level from all families at once. The families above still have levels
and one huge-fanout net that can be cut without touching any stall/CE/clear net (the r13s0 failure) and without
adding load-use or shift latency (the r11s1 / r13s1 failures).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
One theme: every INPUT of the ID forward network (ex_val, mem_ld_val, rs data, the DSP operand ext bit) is
made as shallow and as low-fanout as the flops allow. No new pipeline stage, no new stall, no change to
cycle count (4,065,578 must be unchanged; cosim checks it).

(a) Load value (mem_stage.sv + id_stage.sv). Replace `dmem_rdata >> (addr[1:0]*8)` + width/sext case by an
    explicit one-hot AND-OR whose selects are decoded from the EX/MEM flops (mem_addr[1:0], mem_width,
    mem_sext, mem_to_reg) in parallel with the 2.26 ns BSRAM clock-to-out: lane0..3 for bits [7:0]
    (4-term AND-OR of DO bytes), half/word terms for bits [15:8], and one sign term
    S = sext & (L0&DO[7] | L1&DO[15] | L2&DO[23] | L3&DO[31]) (halfword: DO[15]/DO[31]) for bits [31:8].
    In id_stage the MEM-load term of op1_d/op2_d/rv1_d/rv2_d is fused with the same selects
    (s_mld & lane_k computed early from flops, so DO enters the forward AND-OR directly instead of going
    through a separate mem_ld_val level). Target: DO -> op D in 4 LUT levels instead of 7. The sign term is
    the fanout-24 net; give each of op1/op2/rv1/rv2 its own copy of the 2-LUT sign cone so the net is not
    shared by 4x24 loads.
(b) ex_val (ex_stage.sv). Split `early_masked`: `fwd_val` (the forward value) = alu_fast only; the EX/MEM
    alu_result D keeps `alu_fast | link | div_result`. Mark DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU `late_res` in the ID decode so a
    divide never forwards from EX (a 36-cycle op; the consumer waits one more cycle, ~0 CPI) -- then ex_val
    has no pc+4 incrementer and no divider term at all, and it is exactly the flat one-hot AND-OR of the
    r14s0 sel_* flags. The `ex_fwd` flag already excludes late producers, so function is unchanged.
(c) DSP operand extension (alu.sv, ex_stage.sv, id_stage.sv, core_pkg.sv). The 33rd multiplier bit is
    currently `a[31] & mul_sa` computed after the op flop. Carry two ID/EX flops `mul_a_ext`, `mul_b_ext`
    (D = op1_d[31] & mul_sa_dec / op2_d[31] & mul_sb_dec folded into the existing forward select, i.e.
    `(s1_ex&&!use_pc&&sa ? ex_val[31] : base1[31]&sa)`, same LUT depth as op1_d[31]) and feed the DSP
    {ext, a}. Removes one LUT + its 1.7 ns route from the op1_31 -> DSP -> mul_q leg. Under ALTOPS the ALU
    keeps the original op-decoded behaviour; test_alu.py (PREDEC = 0) is unchanged.
(d) Regfile read selects (if_stage.sv / reg_file.sv). Keep 4 copies of the q0 rs1 and rs2 address fields
    (each copy loaded from the same D as q0[19:15] / q0[24:20], same CE/mux; a copy drives the read mux of 8
    of the 32 data bits, with `(* syn_keep = "true" *)` / `syn_preserve` so Gowin does not merge them). The

    original q0 bits keep driving only decode, fwd_select and the hazard compare. +40 FF, no CE/clear
    net change.

Expected: leg 1 loses ~3 LUT levels (~3 ns), leg 3 disappears, leg 2 loses its OR level and the pc+4 cone,
leg 4 loses a LUT and a long route, leg 5 loses its 4.8 ns net; the remaining tied legs are the carry-chain
compare/adder (op -> redir_q / alu), which are untouched and sit ~0.05 ns below the current wall, so the
median seed should move from 8.90 ns to ~8.4-8.5 ns (112.4 -> ~118-120 MHz). If the compare/adder family then
binds, the gain is smaller; I do not expect a loss because the changes only delete logic levels and
fanout and add ~50 FF.

title: Lane-sliced load-return network: one-hot byte-lane selects registered in EX/MEM, raw BSRAM bytes -> 2-level AND-OR -> ID/EX operand D
motivation:
The CPI side is nearly closed: the 2K -O3 CoreMark run is 2.937M instructions, the 22% imem
stall puts the fetch floor at ~3.77M cycles and the head is at 4.066M, with three loop-replay
variants (r12s2, r13s2, r14s2) buying 2.5-4.7% of cycles at a 7-10% Fmax cost, and r11s1 / r13s1
showing that any extra load/shift consumer latency costs +2.5..5.3% cycles (the 4-deep queue only
recovers ~0.22 slots/cycle). So the remaining lever is Fmax at unchanged cycles.
The experiment table shows which family is the persistent leader once the others are cut: the
dmem BSRAM DO -> load align (mem_stage) -> forward AND-OR (id_stage) -> ID/EX op1/op2 D path
is the logged worst path of r7s2, r8s0, r9s1, r9s2 (the 262 head), r10s1, r11s2, r13s0 and now
of the r14s0 head itself (seed 0: dmem_0 BSRAM -> op2_28, 8 logic cells, arrival 15.45 ns).
The BSRAM clock-to-output is ~5 ns of the 8.9 ns period, so every LUT level after DO is expensive
(~0.5 ns logic + ~1 ns route each) and 8 cells is ~4 more levels than the data dependence needs.
The cause is structural: dmem_rdata goes through `dmem_rdata >> (addr[1:0]*8)`, then a
width/sext `case`, then the id_stage `s_mld & mem_ld_val` AND, then the OR with the other
sources, then the EX-now 2:1 mux -- a serial chain in which every select (addr[1:0], width, sext,
rd compare) is a flop-launched, early signal that is simply not pre-combined.
r10s0 tried this fusion when the DSP / forward-select / is_div / ALU-class legs still tied it
(result flat, 261.80 vs 262.14); r14s0 has since cut exactly those legs (+5.48%) and its own
post-merge report names the BSRAM leg as the leader, which is the precondition that the r10s0
lesson set for a retry.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make the load return a first-class lane-sliced network with all controls decoded one stage
earlier, so the only data-dependent logic after the BSRAM DO pins is a flat AND-OR of four byte
lanes plus one data-dependent sign bit. No cycle-count change, no change to hazard/stall
behaviour, no new pipeline stage.
1. ex_stage: from jalr_sum[1:0] (the low two adder bits, early in the carry chain), mem_width and
   mem_sext compute one-hot load-lane controls and register them in EX/MEM ctrl (set in
   ctrl_with_trap like mem_mis, zero for non-loads and for misaligned loads):
     lo byte  (result[7:0])  : ld_b0 / ld_b1 / ld_b2 / ld_b3  (one-hot: which DO byte lane)
     mid byte (result[15:8]) : ld_m1 (LW, LH@0: lane 1) / ld_m3 (LH@2: lane 3); else ext
     hi bytes (result[23:16], [31:24]) : ld_w (LW only: lanes 2 / 3); else ext
     sign pick: ld_s0..ld_s3 one-hot choosing which lane's bit 7 is the sign (LB@k: lane k,
                LH@0: lane 1, LH@2: lane 3), and ld_sx = sext (zero otherwise).
2. mem_stage: `load_data` (still used for the MEM/WB read_data register and the WB forward term)
   is rebuilt as the flat AND-OR of the four raw lanes with those flop selects (no shifter, no
   width/sext case); it also exports the controls so id_stage can use them.
3. id_stage: the MEM-now load term of the operand network is no longer `{32{s_mld}} & mem_ld_val`.
   Take raw dmem_rdata plus the registered ld_* controls and build, per operand copy (op1 and
   op2 get their own copy of the sign LUT pair so the sign net has fanout ~24, not ~48), the load
   term directly: a_k = s*_mld & ld_bk etc. are computed from flops/compare (early, ~3.5 ns, well
   before DO arrives at ~5+ ns), so after DO there are two LUT levels for the data bytes (LUT4 pair
   (a0&D0 | a1&D1), (a2&D2 | a3&D3), then one LUT5 merging the other sources `base` and the EX-now
   2:1 mux) and three for the sign-extended upper bits. Keep the EX-now term as the last 2:1 mux
   (r14s0 structure) and keep rv1/rv2 (RVFI-only) computed from the same network.
4. core.sv: wire io_dmemRData and the EX/MEM load controls into id_stage; hazard_unit, fwd_select
   (sel_mem_ld semantics), the ID/EX and EX/MEM CE/clear nets are untouched (do NOT split them,
   see r13s0), and no logic is added after the EX/MEM alu_result / mul_q flops or on the fetch
   path (r10s1, r12s2). Under RISCV_FORMAL the behaviour is bit-identical, so riscv-formal
   (pc_fwd, reg, mem checks, ALIGNED_MEM masks) and cosim must pass unchanged.
Why now and why it can clear the 4.6% bar: the other tied families were cut by r14s0 and the
BSRAM leg is the one with the most excess depth (8 cells for a 2-3 level function). If the other
legs sit ~0.4-0.5 ns behind it the gain is ~+3-4% (below the bar), but if the BSRAM leg is the
median-seed wall as it was for r9s2/r13s0/r14s0 seed 0, taking ~4 levels (~4-5 ns of logic plus
routing, with the DO launch fixed) off it moves the median toward the next legs at ~120 MHz
(+5-7%). The risk is that the next-nearest legs (EX-now loop, compare -> redir_q, DSP) are within
~0.3 ns, in which case the result is flat like r10s0.

implementation_notes:
# Lane-sliced load-return network (hyp-20261002-002-r15s1)

## What changed
- `core_pkg.sv`: new `ld_sel_t` (one-hot load-lane selects `b0..b3`, `m1`, `m3`, `w`,
  `s0..s3`, `sb1`, `sb3`), nested in `ctrl_t` as `ctrl.ld` (zero in ID, set in EX like
  `mem_mis`; only the EX/MEM copy is read, the ID/EX and MEM/WB copies are pruned).
- `ex_stage.sv`: decodes `ctrl_with_trap.ld.*` from `jalr_sum[1:0]`, `mem_width`,
  `mem_sext`, `mem_read`. Only aligned loads set anything (every term needs a legal
  width/offset pair), so misaligned loads and non-loads read as 0.
- `ld_term.sv` (new): flat AND-OR of the four raw dmem byte lanes + two sign nets
  (`sign8` for result[15:8], LB only; `sign16` for result[31:16], LB/LH), gated by an
  early `en`. No shifter, no width/sext case.
- `mem_stage.sv`: shifter + width/sext case removed; `load_data` is `ld_term(en=1)`
  (still feeds MEM/WB.read_data and the RVFI-only rv1/rv2 term).
- `id_stage.sv`: new inputs `dmem_rdata`, `mem_ld_sel`. The MEM-now load term of
  op1/op2 is now `ld_term(en = s_mld && !use_const, raw dmem_rdata)`, one instance per
  operand (own sign nets, fanout 8 + 16 instead of ~48). `base1/base2` OR it in; the
  EX-now 2:1 mux stays last. rv1/rv2 (RVFI only, pruned from the timed netlist) still
  use `mem_ld_val`.
- `core.sv`: wires `io_dmemRData` and `ex_mem_w.ctrl.ld` into `u_id`. hazard_unit,
  fwd_select, CE/clear nets untouched.
- `test/test_pipeline.py`: added `ld_term.sv` to the explicit cocotb source list.

## Deviations from the hypothesis
- No separate `ld_sx` flop: sext is folded into the sign picks (`s*`/`sb*` are all zero
  for LBU/LHU/LW).
- Two extra flops `sb1`, `sb3`. A first version (a single `sign` net ORed into
  [15:8] and [31:16]) failed CoreMark: LH of 0x8080 returned 0xFFFFFF80 instead of
  0xFFFF8080 because the sign fill OR'd 0xFF over the LH's own byte 1. Found by diffing
  a CoreMark retirement trace against the baseline core. The [15:8] fill therefore uses
  LB-only selects (`s0, sb1, s2, sb3`) and [31:16] the LB/LH selects (`s0, s1, s2, s3`).
- Nested struct (`ctrl.ld`) rather than 12 flat ctrl_t fields.

## Concerns
- Whether Gowin maps the AND-OR as the intended LUT4 -> LUT5 depth is up to synthesis;
  see the `make timing` result for the worst path.
- 13 extra EX/MEM flops (+ a few LUTs for the decode in EX, off the critical path:
  they hang off jalr_sum[1:0]).

## Status
- verilator lint: clean.
- `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench`: pass (selftest trace + CoreMark CRCs, with stalls).
- local formal (`RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench bash formal/run_all.sh`, auto-detects
  nret=1): 53 passed, 0 failed.
- `pytest cores/bench/test/test_pipeline.py`: pass.
- `make timing TARGET=bench` (place option 0 only): Fmax 113.94 MHz (head in core.yaml: 112.42),
  11 logic levels. The worst paths are now the ALU/EX legs (14.07 ns, op2 -> reg_write / redir_q
  and op1 -> alu_result); the dmem BSRAM -> ID/EX op1 leg (`u_mem/u_ld -> u_id`) is down to
  6 cells / 14.03 ns, 5th in the list, i.e. only ~0.04 ns behind the leader. The BSRAM leg is
  no longer the wall, so further gain has to come from the ALU/compare legs.
- Cycle count is unchanged by construction (no hazard/stall change); CoreMark CRCs pass in cosim.
- Note for reruns: `make formal` passes `checks.cfg` explicitly (nret=2 wrapper); use
  `RTL_DIR=... CORE_NAME=bench bash formal/run_all.sh` and `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench`.
lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-002-r15s1 (regression, -1.56%): Isolating the load-select fusion on the r14s0 head (one-hot byte-lane/sign selects registered in EX/MEM from `jalr_sum[1:0]`/width/sext, a flat `ld_term` AND-OR of raw `dmem_rdata` per operand with its own sign nets, shifter and width/sext case deleted) at unchanged cycles scored 272.20 vs 276.51 even though it did cut the BSRAM -> `op1`/`op2` D leg from 8 cells to 6 (14.03 ns) — the implementer's post-change timing showed the wall had already moved to the ALU/EX legs (`op2` -> `reg_write`/`redir_q` and `op1` -> `alu_result`, 14.07 ns, 11 logic levels) with the load leg only ~0.04 ns behind in 5th place, so this is the third flat/negative load-fusion result (r10s0, r15s0, now r15s1) and the +13 EX/MEM flops/duplicated cones cost more than the leg's slack bought; treat the BSRAM load-return path as closed and aim future Fmax work at the operand-flop -> ALU/compare -> `reg_write`/`redir_q`/`alu_result` cones.

title: Fold predicted direction into registered one-hot branch-resolve flags so compare -> redir_q is a flat AND-OR
motivation:
Measured headroom for any pure-IPC predictor change is small: CoreMark retires ~2.93M instructions in
4.066M cycles, the imem bus delivers at most 100/128 = 0.78 words/cycle (fetch floor ~3.75M cycles), and
the whole redirect cost (~70k redirects x ~2.5 cycles) is only ~3-4% of the run. Bigger/global-history
BHTs (r11s2), a RAS (r7s2) and three loop-replay buffers (r12s2, r13s2, r14s2) all lost because their
Fmax cost exceeded that ceiling. The only predictor-side lever left is Fmax: the resolve end of the
predictor (EX compare -> redirect_raw -> redir_q D) still decodes branch_op through a 6-way case, XORs
with pred_taken, and ANDs three misalign/stall terms after the 32-bit compare, although every one of
those inputs except the compare result itself is known in ID. r14s0 showed that registering encoded
decode fields as one-hot flops pays when it cuts a LUT level from the tied cones; the branch-resolve
cone was left out of that bundle.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep the fetch-side predictor (32x2 bimodal BHT, JAL always taken, zero-bubble taken fetch, registered
redirect, 2-bubble recovery) byte-for-byte, so cycle count stays 4065578. Move the resolve decision into
ID as registered one-hot "redirect-if" flags. In id_stage, from the decoder branch_op, the FD-head
in.pred_taken and the opcode/immediate bits, compute and register in ID/EX ctrl: rd_eq, rd_ne, rd_lt,
rd_ge, rd_ltu, rd_geu, rd_one. rd_x means "redirect when comparator output x is true", with the
predicted direction already folded in (BEQ predicted not-taken -> rd_eq; BEQ predicted taken -> rd_ne;
BLT predicted not-taken -> rd_lt; BLT predicted taken -> rd_ge; ...; JALR (never predicted) and JAL with
pred_taken=0 -> rd_one). The misaligned-target gate is also folded in ID: a branch/JAL whose static
target has imm[1]=1 is never predicted, so all its flags are forced to 0 (redirect suppressed, as now).
Only the dynamic JALR misalign term (jalr_sum[1], low-bits adder) stays as a late AND.
In ex_stage, redirect_raw becomes
  ((eq & rd_eq) | (~eq & rd_ne) | (lt & rd_lt) | (~lt & rd_ge) | (ltu & rd_ltu) | (~ltu & rd_geu) | rd_one)
  & ~jalr_mis & ~redir_q & ~stall
with eq/lt/ltu the three raw comparator outputs, so the 6:1 branch_op case, the pred_taken XOR and the
misalign_branch/misalign_jump terms disappear from the compare->redir_q D cone (~2 LUT levels removed
from the cone that ends at a single flop). The existing branch_taken (for BHT training / pc_next /
RVFI) is left as is; it is not on the redir_q D pin. redirect_target_d keeps its registered-select
structure (pred_taken ? pc+4 : is_jalr ? jalr_sum : pc+imm). Because the flags are folded in ID from q0
flops, nothing is added to the fetch/imem_data -> predecode -> pc cone or to the stall/CE nets (ID/EX
ctrl flops use the same flush/!stall enables as today: no split control sets, avoiding the r13s0
failure mode). Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS nothing changes (ALU-only difference), so formal exercises
the same redirect semantics; cosim must stay cycle-identical to 4065578. Expected effect: pure Fmax,
+2-4% if the compare->redir_q family is among the tied wall legs, ~0 otherwise (area +7 FF).

changes.description: Add rd_eq/rd_ne/rd_lt/rd_ge/rd_ltu/rd_geu/rd_one redirect-if flags to ctrl_t (zero for non-branch/jump).

Compute the redirect-if one-hot flags from branch_op, in.pred_taken, is_branch/is_jump/is_jalr and the static target-misalign bits (instr[8] for B, instr[21] for JAL); register them in ID/EX ctrl under the existing flush/!stall enables.

Rebuild redirect_raw as a flat AND-OR of the raw comparator outputs (eq, lt, ltu) and the registered flags, gated only by ~jalr_mis (jalr_sum[1]) & ~redir_q & ~stall; keep branch_taken for BHT training, pc_next and RVFI unchanged.
Add rd_eq/rd_ne/rd_lt/rd_ge/rd_ltu/rd_geu/rd_one redirect-if flags to ctrl_t (zero for non-branch/jump).

Compute the redirect-if one-hot flags from branch_op, in.pred_taken, is_branch/is_jump/is_jalr and the static target-misalign bits (instr[8] for B, instr[21] for JAL); register them in ID/EX ctrl under the existing flush/!stall enables.

Rebuild redirect_raw as a flat AND-OR of the raw comparator outputs (eq, lt, ltu) and the registered flags, gated only by ~jalr_mis (jalr_sum[1]) & ~redir_q & ~stall; keep branch_taken for BHT training, pc_next and RVFI unchanged.

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-003-r15s2 (regression, -3.62%): Folding the predicted direction, branch op and static-target misalign gate into seven registered one-hot ID/EX `rd_eq/ne/lt/ge/ltu/geu/one` flags so `redirect_raw` became a flat AND-OR of the raw `cmp_eq`/`cmp_lt`/`cmp_ltu` outputs (6:1 `branch_op` case, `pred_taken` XOR and `misalign_*` terms gone from the compare -> `redir_q` D cone) scored 266.50 vs the 276.51 r14s0 head against a predicted +3%, even though r15s1's timing had named `op2` -> `redir_q` as a binding wall leg — a registered-decode cut to a leg that already ends at one D pin (r6s1) did not move Fmax, and the new decode cone off the FD-head `pred_taken`/`raw_instr` flops into 7 more ID/EX ctrl flops (+7 FF on the shared flush/!stall enables) plus three always-parallel full-width comparators in place of the `branch_op`-muxed compares are the unverified suspects (no post-change `make timing` or cycle count captured) — this is the fourth narrow level-cut on the r14s0 wall to lose (r14s1 -0.54%, r15s0 -4.34%, r15s1 -1.56%), so don't re-propose registered branch-resolve flags standalone and require a post-change path report showing the `redir_q` leg is the one still binding.
